package loom // import "ubunatic.com/loom"

Package loom is an inline terminal UI library.

A Pane reserves a fixed-height region below the shell cursor, renders a Widget
tree into a Canvas on every frame, and dispatches keyboard and mouse events.
The terminal is always restored on exit, panic, or signal.

Typical usage:

    items := []loom.Item{{Name: "git"}, {Name: "make"}}
    choice := loom.NewChoice(items)
    pane, err := loom.New(12)
    if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
    defer pane.Close()
    pane.Run(choice)
    if item, ok := choice.Selected(); ok {
        fmt.Println(item.Name)
    }

See docs/TuiInput.md for the constraints that govern /dev/tty usage, EINTR
handling, and ZSH widget compatibility.

CONSTANTS

const (
	ModeOvertype = AnsiModeOvertype
	ModeInsert   = AnsiModeInsert
)
    Aliases for convenience and compatibility.


VARIABLES

var Debug bool
    Debug is a package-level flag. When enabled, containers draw dotted cell
    outlines.

var DebugColor = ColorIndex(242)
    DebugColor is the Color used for debug boundaries. Defaults to a medium grey
    (ColorIndex(242)).

var DefaultMaxCols = SpeccedDefaults.Pane.MaxCols
    DefaultMaxCols is the default maximum canvas width loaded from
    SpeccedDefaults.

var DefaultPlaceholder = SpeccedDefaults.Choice.DefaultPlaceholder
    DefaultPlaceholder is the search-bar hint of Choice and Table.

var Reset = Style{}
    Reset is a zero Style — default terminal colors, no attributes.

var SpeccedBackground = loadBackgroundDefaults()
var SpeccedCursorPressPulse = func() CursorPressPulseSpec {
	var spec cursorSpecFile
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(cursorSpecYAML, &spec); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: parse spec/cursor.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	pulse := spec.PressPulse
	pulse.Lifetime = time.Duration(pulse.LifetimeMS) * time.Millisecond
	pulse.Frame = time.Duration(pulse.FrameMS) * time.Millisecond
	return pulse
}()
    SpeccedCursorPressPulse is the immutable expanding press effect config.

var SpeccedCursorProximity = func() CursorProximitySpec {
	var spec cursorSpecFile
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(cursorSpecYAML, &spec); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: parse spec/cursor.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	return spec.Proximity
}()
    SpeccedCursorProximity is the immutable proximity effect configuration.

var SpeccedCursorStarTrail = func() CursorStarTrailSpec {
	var spec cursorSpecFile
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(cursorSpecYAML, &spec); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: parse spec/cursor.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	trail := spec.StarTrail
	trail.Lifetime = time.Duration(trail.LifetimeMS) * time.Millisecond
	trail.Frame = time.Duration(trail.FrameMS) * time.Millisecond
	return trail
}()
    SpeccedCursorStarTrail is the immutable star trail effect configuration.

var SpeccedDefaults = func() LibDefaults {
	var defs LibDefaults
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(defaultsYAML, &defs); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: parse spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Scrollbar.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Mouse.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.ColorPicker.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.RichTextEdit.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.NumberInput.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Toggle.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Paginator.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Tree.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Split.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := defs.Choice.validate(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/defaults.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	return defs
}()
    SpeccedDefaults holds the loaded immutable defaults from spec/defaults.yaml.

var SpeccedResizeModeIDs = append([]string(nil), SpeccedResizeModes.ModeOrder...)
    SpeccedResizeModeIDs lists all mode identifiers in fixed presentation order.

var SpeccedResizeModes = func() ResizeModesSpec {
	var spec ResizeModesSpec
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(resizeSpecYAML, &spec); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: parse spec/resize.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if err := spec.validateModeOrder(); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: spec/resize.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	for id, m := range spec.Modes {
		m.ID = id
		spec.Modes[id] = m
	}
	if a := spec.Modes["adaptive_guard"]; a.MinN > a.MaxN || a.WindowMS <= 0 || a.RateStep <= 0 {
		panic("loom: spec/resize.yaml adaptive_guard needs window_ms > 0, rate_step > 0 and min_n <= max_n")
	}
	return spec
}()
    SpeccedResizeModes is the loaded immutable spec of resize modes.

var SpeccedThemes = func() map[string]ThemeColors {
	var f themesFile
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(themesYAML, &f); err != nil {
		panic(fmt.Sprintf("loom: parse spec/themes.yaml: %v", err))
	}
	if _, ok := f.Themes["plain"]; !ok {
		panic("loom: spec/themes.yaml: required base theme \"plain\" is missing")
	}
	return f.Themes
}()
    SpeccedThemes holds all themes loaded from spec/themes.yaml at init time.
    Keys are theme names ("plain", "mc", …).

var Version = "0.3.10"

FUNCTIONS

func ActiveModalMouse(root Widget) (Widget, Rect)
    ActiveModalMouse resolves a widget's modal contract, including transparent
    WidgetUnwrapper wrappers. Containers expose only their visible children.

func AdaptiveGuardN(rate float64, events, manualN int) int
    AdaptiveGuardN maps a measured rate (with its event count) to a guard width
    using the spec policy: min_n + floor(rate/rate_step), clamped to max_n. With
    fewer than two events there is no measurable speed, so it returns manualN.

func BoxGlyph(arms BoxArms) string
    BoxGlyph returns the light box-drawing glyph represented by arms.

func BuildWidget(r io.Reader) (Widget, *YamlConfig, error)
    BuildWidget parses YAML configuration and constructs the widget tree and
    Router without opening a terminal. Safe to call in tests and headless
    environments.

func BuildWidgetFile(path string) (Widget, *YamlConfig, error)
    BuildWidgetFile reads a .loom.yaml file and constructs the widget tree
    without opening a terminal.

func ClipRow(row string, width int) string
    ClipRow hard-clips row to at most width real terminal columns, regardless
    of what width the caller's renderer (e.g. graph.RenderTreemap) was asked
    to produce -- renderers only know the width they were told, never the
    terminal's actual live width, so this is where that gets reconciled against
    reality.

    Escape sequences are copied through untouched (they cost zero screen
    columns) so inline color/style survives clipping -- that is the one thing
    a drawing component is allowed to emit into its rows; see RawScreen's doc
    comment. A trailing reset ("\x1b[0m") is appended whenever any styling was
    seen, so a row clipped mid-style can never bleed its color into whatever is
    drawn next.

func DecodeMouse(b []byte) (MouseEvent, bool)
    DecodeMouse parses an SGR (\x1b[<…M or \x1b[<…m) mouse report. Returns
    (event, true) on success, (zero, false) if b is not an SGR mouse report.

func DecodePaste(b []byte) (PasteEvent, int, bool)
    DecodePaste decodes a complete bracketed-paste frame at the start of b.

func DefaultEditorConfigPath() string
    DefaultEditorConfigPath returns the XDG config path for editor.yaml
    (~/.config/loom/editor.yaml).

func DisplayPath(path string) string
    DisplayPath formats a path for safe terminal display.

func DrawRuler(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    DrawRuler frames r with a 1-cell ruler on the terminal's default background,
    so cells a snapshot leaves unpainted show through next to it.

func FormatPillCluster(pills []ProviderPill, gap int, useANSI bool) string
    FormatPillCluster returns an ANSI-formatted string of the pill cluster.

func IsMarkupPath(path string) bool
    IsMarkupPath reports whether path names a .tui markup file.

func KeyCap(binding string) string
    KeyCap renders a binding such as ctrl-alt-s as a keycap label such as ⌃⌥S.
    Modifier glyphs and their order come from the spec (keycaps.modifiers),
    so every hint bar, menu and help text shows the same caps.

func MarkupImageMaxSize() (width, height int)
    MarkupImageMaxSize returns the largest image size in cells that an image tag
    may request (spec/markup.yaml). Image hooks cap the native image size by it
    when width and height are unset.

func OpenFile(path string) error
    OpenFile launches path with the current platform's desktop file opener.

func ParseYAML(r io.Reader) (Widget, *Pane, error)
    ParseYAML reads YAML configuration from a reader and builds the TUI layout
    with view routing.

func ParseYAMLFile(path string) (Widget, *Pane, error)
    ParseYAMLFile reads a .loom.yaml file and constructs the widget tree and
    Pane.

func QuoteUnprintable(value string) string
    QuoteUnprintable returns value unchanged when every rune is printable and an
    ASCII-escaped, quoted representation otherwise.

func Render(root Widget, cols, rows int) []string
    Render draws root into an off-screen canvas of the given size and returns
    each row as an ANSI string (styles reset at every row end, matching
    Canvas.Row). It opens no terminal, so it is safe in headless contexts,
    tests, and screenshots.

func RenderTo(w io.Writer, root Widget, cols, rows int) error
    RenderTo draws one off-screen frame and writes it as sequential lines to w.
    It performs no terminal control, making it suitable for non-interactive
    previews, redirected output, and tests. cols and rows must be positive.

func RunPane(w Paneable) (item Item, ok bool, nav Nav, err error)
    RunPane opens an inline Pane sized to w, runs w's event loop, and always
    closes the pane before returning — so the terminal is restored (and the
    reserved region cleared) before the caller writes any result to stdout.

    It returns the selection, the ok flag from w.Selected (false when the user
    aborted), and the widget's navigation signal. A non-nil error means the pane
    could not be opened or the event loop failed; on error item/ok/nav are zero.

    RunPane is the exported form of the open/run/close dance shown in the
    package doc. Terminal restore on SIGINT/SIGTERM and panic is handled by Pane
    itself.

func RuneWidth(r rune) int
    RuneWidth returns the visual column width of a single rune.

func SaveAnsiBuffer(buf *AnsiBuffer, path string) error
    SaveAnsiBuffer writes an AnsiBuffer to path.

func ScreenshotScript(rows []string, comment string) string
    ScreenshotScript turns rendered ANSI rows into a minimal, self-printing bash
    script: running it replays the captured frame with its original colors.

    It is a testing/debugging utility (pair it with Render to capture a frame
    without a terminal), not part of the interactive widget API. Each row is
    emitted as a single-quoted argument to one printf, with ESC bytes written
    as \033 and embedded single quotes escaped, so the file stays plain 7-bit
    text with no raw control characters. The comment is placed in a header
    line (newlines collapsed) to identify the shot. Line 2 is always `set -euo
    pipefail`, as docs/Bash.md requires.

func SerializeAnsiBuffer(buf *AnsiBuffer) string
    SerializeAnsiBuffer converts an AnsiBuffer to an ANSI formatted string.

func StringWidth(s string) int
    StringWidth returns the visual column width of a string.

func TerminalSize() (cols, rows int, err error)
    TerminalSize returns the dimensions of the controlling terminal. It returns
    an error when /dev/tty is unavailable or its size cannot be read.

func ThemeExists(name string) bool
    ThemeExists reports whether name is a theme loaded from spec/themes.yaml.

func ThemeNames() []string
    ThemeNames returns the names of all themes loaded from spec/themes.yaml,
    sorted in ascending order.

func TruncateText(text string, width int, marker string) string
    TruncateText fits text to a terminal-cell budget, adding the caller's marker
    only when truncation is needed. It follows Canvas's supported text policy:
    terminal instructions are stripped, combining marks stay with their base,
    and wide glyphs are never split. Pass styles separately through Style.
    A marker wider than the budget is itself clipped, without recursive markers.

func TruncateTextLeft(text string, width int, marker string) string
    TruncateTextLeft fits text to a terminal-cell budget by truncating leading
    clusters, keeping trailing characters and prepending the caller's marker
    when truncated. It follows the same supported text policy as TruncateText.

func ValidateAnsiBox(text string) error
    ValidateAnsiBox checks that rows which form a Unicode box have consistent
    visual widths and aligned left and right borders. Text without box drawing
    characters is accepted unchanged.

func ValidateEditorConfigYAML(data []byte) error
    ValidateEditorConfigYAML validates raw YAML bytes against
    spec/schemas/editor.schema.json.

func ValidateYAML(r io.Reader) error
    ValidateYAML decodes and validates a Loom YAML layout configuration stream.

func WriteOSC52(w io.Writer, text string) error
    WriteOSC52 writes an OSC 52 clipboard request containing text to w.

func WriteRows(out io.Writer, rows []string) error
    WriteRows writes rows to out as plain, sequential, newline-terminated lines,
    at wherever the cursor already is -- like any ordinary command's output.
    This is the right primitive for a one-shot "print once and exit" path:
    it must never touch cursor position or full-screen state, or it will clobber
    whatever the shell (prompt, prior scrollback) already put on screen above
    it.

    When out is a real terminal, each row is still clipped (ClipRow) to the
    terminal's live width first, so a single over-wide row can't wrap and
    misalign -- but that's the only terminal-state concern a one-shot print has.
    Anything more (hiding the cursor, disabling auto-wrap, absolute positioning)
    belongs to RawScreen, and only to a genuine redraw loop; see RawScreen's
    doc comment for why applying that to a one-shot print is itself a bug,
    not extra safety.


TYPES

type Align int
    Align controls text alignment within a column.

const (
	AlignLeft Align = iota
	AlignRight
)
type AlignBox struct {
	Child  Widget
	HAlign layout.Align
	VAlign layout.Align
	Width  int // explicit content width; 0 derives from child
	Height int // explicit content height; 0 derives from child
}
    AlignBox is a container widget that positions its child according to
    horizontal and vertical alignment rules within the allocated Canvas
    rectangle.

func NewAlign(child Widget, hAlign, vAlign layout.Align) *AlignBox
    NewAlign creates an AlignBox widget with specific horizontal and vertical
    alignments.

func NewCenter(child Widget) *AlignBox
    NewCenter creates an AlignBox widget that centers its child both
    horizontally and vertically.

func (a *AlignBox) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey delegates key events to the child widget.

func (a *AlignBox) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse delegates mouse events to the child widget.

func (a *AlignBox) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the child height.

func (a *AlignBox) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth estimates the child width.

func (a *AlignBox) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders Child within r, offset by the computed alignment margins.
    Out-of-bounds or zero space is handled safely without drawing outside r.

func (a *AlignBox) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure implements Measurer.

type AnimatedBackground interface {
	Background
	DrawBackgroundAt(*Canvas, Rect, time.Time)
}
    AnimatedBackground is a background that needs periodic redraws.

type AnsiBuffer struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    AnsiBuffer is an in-memory 2D cell grid for ANSI art editing and terminal
    graphics.

func LoadAnsiBuffer(path string, defaultCols, defaultRows int) (*AnsiBuffer, error)
    LoadAnsiBuffer reads an ANSI file and parses it into a 2D AnsiBuffer. If the
    file does not exist, an empty buffer with default dimensions is returned.

func NewAnsiBuffer(cols, rows int) *AnsiBuffer
    NewAnsiBuffer creates an empty ANSI buffer with the specified columns and
    rows.

func ParseAnsiBuffer(content string, minCols, minRows int) (*AnsiBuffer, error)
    ParseAnsiBuffer parses an ANSI string into a 2D AnsiBuffer.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Backspace(x, y int, mode AnsiEditMode) int
    Backspace handles backspace at cursor (x, y). Returns the new cursor x
    coordinate.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Clipboard() (AnsiCell, bool)
    Clipboard returns the current clipboard content and whether it is populated.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Cols() int
    Cols returns the buffer width.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Copy(x, y int) AnsiCell
    Copy copies the cell at (x, y) to the internal clipboard.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Cut(x, y int) AnsiCell
    Cut copies the cell at (x, y) and erases it.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Delete(x, y int, mode AnsiEditMode)
    Delete deletes the character at (x, y). In insert mode, shifts remaining
    characters on the line left by 1. In overtype mode, replaces with blank.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Erase(x, y int)
    Erase resets the cell at (x, y) to blank.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Get(x, y int) AnsiCell
    Get returns the cell at (x, y), or BlankAnsiCell if out of bounds.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Modified() bool
    Modified returns true if the buffer has unsaved changes.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) NextObjectRow(y int) int
    NextObjectRow finds the next non-empty block / object row below y.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) NextWord(x, y int) int
    NextWord finds the next word boundary to the right on line y starting from
    x.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Paste(x, y int) bool
    Paste pastes the clipboard cell at (x, y) if clipboard is non-empty.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Path() string
    Path returns the buffer file path.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) PlainText() string
    PlainText converts the buffer contents to plain text without styling or
    escape sequences.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) PrevObjectRow(y int) int
    PrevObjectRow finds the previous non-empty block / object row above y.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) PrevWord(x, y int) int
    PrevWord finds the previous word boundary to the left on line y starting
    from x.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Put(x, y int, r rune, fg, bg Color, bold, dim, underline, invert bool)
    Put writes a character with given styles at (x, y).

func (b *AnsiBuffer) PutChar(x, y int, r rune, fg, bg Color, bold, dim, underline, invert bool, mode AnsiEditMode)
    PutChar writes a character at (x, y) respecting the current edit mode.
    In insert mode, characters to the right on the same row are shifted right.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Resize(newCols, newRows int)
    Resize resizes the buffer grid, preserving existing cells.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Rows() int
    Rows returns the buffer height.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) SaveFile(path string) error
    SaveFile writes the ANSI buffer contents to path.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Serialize() string
    Serialize converts the buffer contents to an ANSI formatted string.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) Set(x, y int, cell AnsiCell)
    Set places a cell at (x, y) if within bounds.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) SetClipboard(cell AnsiCell)
    SetClipboard sets the buffer's clipboard cell directly.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) SetModified(m bool)
    SetModified sets the modified state.

func (b *AnsiBuffer) SetPath(p string)
    SetPath sets the buffer file path.

type AnsiCell struct {
	Rune      rune
	FG        Color
	BG        Color
	Bold      bool
	Dim       bool
	Underline bool
	Invert    bool
}
    AnsiCell represents a single styled character cell in a 2D ANSI buffer grid.

func BlankAnsiCell() AnsiCell
    BlankAnsiCell returns a default empty cell with reset styling.

func (c AnsiCell) IsBlank() bool
    IsBlank reports whether the cell contains whitespace and default colors
    without attributes.

func (c AnsiCell) Style() Style
    Style converts AnsiCell formatting to Style.

func (c AnsiCell) ToCell() Cell
    ToCell converts AnsiCell to Cell.

func (c AnsiCell) ToLoomCell() Cell
    ToLoomCell is an alias for ToCell for backwards compatibility.

type AnsiEditMode int
    AnsiEditMode represents character insertion vs overtype behavior in an ANSI
    buffer.

const (
	AnsiModeOvertype AnsiEditMode = iota
	AnsiModeInsert
)
func (m AnsiEditMode) String() string

type AnsiEditor struct {
	Buffer *AnsiBuffer

	// Cursor position within the buffer
	CursorX int
	CursorY int

	// Viewport scroll offset
	ScrollX int
	ScrollY int

	// Active styling for new characters
	ActiveFG        Color
	ActiveBG        Color
	ActiveBold      bool
	ActiveDim       bool
	ActiveUnderline bool
	ActiveInvert    bool

	// Active editing mode
	EditMode AnsiEditMode

	ShowCursor bool

	// Optional callbacks
	OnChange     func(buf *AnsiBuffer)
	OnCursorMove func(x, y int)
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    AnsiEditor is an interactive 2D ANSI graphic cell editor widget.
    It embeds an AnsiBuffer and provides viewport scrolling, cursor navigation,
    overtype/insert text editing, and styled cell mutations.

func NewAnsiEditor(buf *AnsiBuffer) *AnsiEditor
    NewAnsiEditor creates a new AnsiEditor for the given buffer. If buf is nil,
    an empty default buffer (80x24) is created.

func (e *AnsiEditor) ConsumeKey(ke KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey processes keyboard input, returning an EventResult value struct.

func (e *AnsiEditor) ConsumeMouse(me MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse processes mouse input, returning an EventResult value struct.

func (e *AnsiEditor) Cursor() (x, y int)
    Cursor returns the current cursor coordinates (x, y).

func (e *AnsiEditor) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the visible viewport of the ANSI buffer and the cursor into
    canvas region r.

func (e *AnsiEditor) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the editor has keyboard focus.

func (e *AnsiEditor) PaneRequest() PaneRequest
    PaneRequest declares terminal capabilities needed by AnsiEditor.

func (e *AnsiEditor) SetCursor(x, y int)
    SetCursor moves the cursor to (x, y), clamping to valid buffer bounds.

func (e *AnsiEditor) SetFocus(f bool)
    SetFocus sets the editor focus state.

type AstraBackground struct{}
    AstraBackground renders a deterministic, slowly changing star field.

func NewAstraBackground() *AstraBackground
    NewAstraBackground returns the spec-driven Astra star field background.

func (AstraBackground) BackgroundInterval() time.Duration

func (AstraBackground) DrawBackground(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    DrawBackground renders one Astra animation frame.

func (AstraBackground) DrawBackgroundAt(c *Canvas, r Rect, now time.Time)
    DrawBackgroundAt renders a deterministic frame at now. Cell placement and
    glyph selection are stable; only the visibility phase changes over time.

type AutoFullscreenSpec struct {
	Title       string `yaml:"title"`
	Description string `yaml:"description"`
	Default     bool   `yaml:"default"`
	Key         string `yaml:"key"`
	ByWidth     bool   `yaml:"by_width"`
	ByHeight    bool   `yaml:"by_height"`
	MarginCols  int    `yaml:"margin_cols"`
	MarginRows  int    `yaml:"margin_rows"`
	MinPercent  int    `yaml:"min_percent"`
	Alt         bool   `yaml:"alt"`
	LeakGuard   bool   `yaml:"leak_guard"`
}
    AutoFullscreenSpec declares quasi-fullscreen detection (see
    QuasiFullscreen).

type Background interface {
	DrawBackground(*Canvas, Rect)
}
    Background paints behind a widget tree. Backgrounds must only write inside
    the supplied rectangle; Pane invokes them before the foreground widget.

type BackgroundCadence interface {
	BackgroundInterval() time.Duration
}
    BackgroundCadence optionally lets an animated background choose its redraw
    interval. Implementations that do not provide it use the spec default.

type Box struct {
	ID         string    `yaml:"id"`
	Title      string    `yaml:"title"`
	Width      int       `yaml:"width"`
	Height     int       `yaml:"height"`
	Dynamic    bool      `yaml:"dynamic"`
	FillHeight bool      `yaml:"fill_height"`
	MinWidth   int       `yaml:"min_width"`
	MaxWidth   int       `yaml:"max_width"`
	MinHeight  int       `yaml:"min_height"`
	MaxHeight  int       `yaml:"max_height"`
	Padding    int       `yaml:"padding"`
	Border     BoxBorder `yaml:"-"`
	Style      BoxStyle  `yaml:"-"`
	Child      Widget    `yaml:"-"`
	Hidden     bool      `yaml:"hidden"`
	Footer     string    `yaml:"footer"`
	Rows       *Rows     `yaml:"rows"`

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Box is a titled border with padding and an optional isolated child. Width
    and Height are preferred outer dimensions used by Frame. YAML frames load
    Border from Loom's embedded spec; Go callers supply it.

func (b *Box) ConsumeKey(k KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey forwards input to the child, if present.

func (b *Box) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse forwards events inside the last drawn child bounds.

func (b *Box) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw paints a box. Bounds smaller than a complete border are left blank.

func (b *Box) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure returns the preferred outer size of the box, including border,
    padding, title/footer and known child content. A positive width wraps the
    child content before calculating its height.

func (b *Box) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget exposes a visible child modal before border hit-testing.

func (b *Box) SetRowsValues(values [][]string)
    SetRowsValues updates the box's rows values dynamically if rows are present.

type BoxArms uint8
    BoxArms identifies the connected sides of a light box-drawing glyph.

const (
	BoxArmUp BoxArms = 1 << iota
	BoxArmRight
	BoxArmDown
	BoxArmLeft
)
func BoxGlyphArms(glyph string) BoxArms
    BoxGlyphArms returns the connected sides of a light box-drawing glyph.

type BoxBorder struct {
	TopLeft     string `yaml:"top_left"`
	TopRight    string `yaml:"top_right"`
	BottomLeft  string `yaml:"bottom_left"`
	BottomRight string `yaml:"bottom_right"`
	Horizontal  string `yaml:"horizontal"`
	Vertical    string `yaml:"vertical"`
	TitlePrefix string `yaml:"title_prefix"`
	TitleSuffix string `yaml:"title_suffix"`
	// Joints for dividers, used by .tui tables: ┬ ┴ ├ ┤ ┼.
	TeeTop    string `yaml:"tee_top"`
	TeeBottom string `yaml:"tee_bottom"`
	TeeLeft   string `yaml:"tee_left"`
	TeeRight  string `yaml:"tee_right"`
	Cross     string `yaml:"cross"`
}
    BoxBorder specifies the one-cell border glyphs and title decoration.

type BoxBorderStyle int
    BoxBorderStyle specifies which glyph set to use for drawing borders. Values:
    Sharp (┌─┐│└┘), Rounded (╭─╮│╰╯), Double (╔═╗║╚╝), ASCII (+-+||++)

const (
	BoxBorderStyleSharp BoxBorderStyle = iota
	BoxBorderStyleRounded
	BoxBorderStyleDouble
	BoxBorderStyleASCII
)
func ParseBoxBorderStyle(s string) (BoxBorderStyle, error)
    ParseBoxBorderStyle parses a string into a BoxBorderStyle.

func (s BoxBorderStyle) String() string
    String returns the name of the border style.

type BoxStyle struct {
	Background Style
	Border     Style
	Title      Style
	Footer     Style
}
    BoxStyle controls a box's background, border, title, and footer.

type Cadence struct {
	Collect time.Duration
	Redraw  time.Duration
}
    Cadence configures independent collection and rendering intervals. Callbacks
    execute serially: drawing must only read the latest collected state.
    Collection should be bounded; slow external I/O belongs outside this loop.

func (c Cadence) Run(ctx context.Context, collect func(time.Time) error, draw func() error) error
    Run collects and draws initially, then runs each callback at its own
    cadence. Cancellation and callback errors stop both timers before returning.
    Missed ticks coalesce; redraws never synthesize samples or advance collected
    history.

func (c Cadence) Validate() error
    Validate rejects intervals that cannot drive a ticker.

type Canvas struct {

	// ColorProfile is captured when the canvas is created and controls SGR output.
	ColorProfile ColorProfile

	CursorX        int // 0-based column index, -1 if hidden
	CursorY        int // 0-based row index, -1 if hidden
	CursorShape    CursorShape
	CursorShapeSet bool
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Canvas is a 2-D frame buffer. Widgets draw into it; Pane flushes it to the
    terminal.

func NewCanvas(cols, rows int) *Canvas
    NewCanvas allocates a cols×rows canvas filled with blank cells.

func (c *Canvas) ApplyCursorBrighten()
    ApplyCursorBrighten brightens backgrounds, including those behind text.
    Terminal-default backgrounds have no resolvable RGB value and remain as-is.

func (c *Canvas) ApplyCursorPulse(pulse CursorPulse, now time.Time) bool
    ApplyCursorPulse paints the expanding ring and reports whether another frame
    remains active. Unresolvable terminal-default backgrounds are left alone.

func (c *Canvas) ApplyCursorStarTrail(points []CursorTrailPoint, now time.Time)
    ApplyCursorStarTrail draws unexpired cursor trail points, newest last.
    When the cell background is terminal-default and has no RGB value, the star
    fades toward black.

func (c *Canvas) Blit(src *Canvas, dstX, dstY int)
    Blit copies src into c with its top-left corner at (dstX, dstY). The copy is
    clipped to c's bounds; wide glyphs are copied only when both cells fit.

func (c *Canvas) Bounds() Rect
    Bounds returns a Rect covering the full canvas.

func (c *Canvas) Clear()
    Clear resets every cell in the canvas to blank and hides the cursor.
    The cursor is reset each frame so a widget that wants it visible must set
    it during Draw; otherwise a prompt-less page (e.g. a View) would inherit
    a stale cursor position from the previous frame and leave a stray block on
    screen.

func (c *Canvas) ClearCursorPosition()
    ClearCursorPosition removes the cursor hint, such as before the first motion
    report or after a report outside the pane.

func (c *Canvas) ClearRect(r Rect)
    ClearRect resets cells in r without inheriting their previous surface style.

func (c *Canvas) Cols() int
    Cols returns the canvas width.

func (c *Canvas) ComposeBackground(background Background, area Rect, now time.Time)
    ComposeBackground renders a background only into cells not claimed by the
    foreground pass. The canvas cursor is restored even if the effect changes it
    accidentally, keeping cursor ownership with the foreground renderer.

func (c *Canvas) CursorHintAt(x, y int) (CursorHint, bool)
    CursorHintAt returns a relative hint for positions within the spec radius.

func (c *Canvas) DrawBorder(r Rect, style BoxBorderStyle, s Style)
    DrawBorder paints the border of a rectangle using the specified style.
    The border is clipped to the canvas bounds. Rectangles smaller than 2×2 are
    not drawn.

func (c *Canvas) DrawBox(r Rect, style BoxBorderStyle, title string, s Style)
    DrawBox paints a border with an optional left-aligned title. The title is
    display-width aware and truncated with an ellipsis (…) if it does not fit.
    Multi-byte runes and combining marks are never split. Rectangles smaller
    than 2×2 are not drawn.

func (c *Canvas) Fill(r Rect, cell Cell)
    Fill fills the rectangle r with cell. Clips to canvas bounds.

func (c *Canvas) Flush(out interface{ WriteString(string) (int, error) }, startRow int)
    Flush writes all rows to out using absolute cursor positioning. startRow is
    the 1-based terminal row of the canvas top-left corner.

func (c *Canvas) FlushWithClear(out interface{ WriteString(string) (int, error) }, startRow, clearRows int)
    FlushWithClear writes the complete canvas as one synchronized terminal
    update using the default resize rendering configuration. clearRows requests
    additional rows below the canvas to be erased; this is used when a resize
    shrinks the pane without exposing a blank intermediate frame.

func (c *Canvas) FlushWithConfig(out interface{ WriteString(string) (int, error) }, startRow, clearRows int, cfg ResizeConfig)
    FlushWithConfig writes the canvas to out with the provided resize rendering
    switches (atomic buffered flush, per-row clearing, synchronized output).

func (c *Canvas) Get(x, y int) Cell
    Get returns the cell at (x, y), or blank for out-of-bounds coordinates.

func (c *Canvas) IsEligibleBackground(x, y int) bool
    IsEligibleBackground reports whether a cell may be filled by a background
    compositor. Cells written by the foreground, wide-rune continuations,
    and the active cursor are protected.

func (c *Canvas) PaintDecoration(x, y int, cell Cell)
    PaintDecoration paints only into cells available to the decoration layer.
    It is safe to call during or outside ComposeBackground.

func (c *Canvas) PaintDefaultSurface(r Rect, style Style)
    PaintDefaultSurface is a weak version of PaintSurface: it skips cells that
    already carry an explicit surface paint (Surface flag set and BG non-reset),
    preserving a parent's PaintSurface (e.g. Grid FocusBG or an ambient canvas
    background). Cells with foreground content or no surface are overwritten,
    clearing stale content from a previous frame. When a widget is drawn
    standalone on a blank canvas the default surface shows the theme's normal
    background, satisfying ticket 222. Explicit surfaces such as Dialog and
    Popup should use PaintSurface instead.

func (c *Canvas) PaintForeground(x, y int, cell Cell)
    PaintForeground paints content that owns its cell, including an explicitly
    blank cell via Claim.

func (c *Canvas) PaintSurface(r Rect, style Style)
    PaintSurface paints a background surface without claiming its cells from the
    decoration layer.

func (c *Canvas) Row(y int) string
    Row renders row y as an ANSI string, resetting style at the end. Returns an
    empty string for out-of-range rows.

func (c *Canvas) Rows() int
    Rows returns the canvas height.

func (c *Canvas) Set(x, y int, cell Cell)
    Set places a single cell at (x, y). Out-of-bounds writes are silently
    dropped.

func (c *Canvas) SetCursorPosition(x, y int)

func (c *Canvas) SubCanvas(r Rect) *Canvas
    SubCanvas returns an independent canvas containing the requested region.
    Its local origin (0, 0) corresponds to (r.X, r.Y) in c. Cells outside c's
    bounds remain blank, and changes to the returned canvas do not affect c.

func (c *Canvas) Write(x, y int, text string, style Style) int
    Write renders text starting at (x, y) using style, advancing x for each
    rune. Returns the number of columns consumed. Clips at canvas right edge.
    Correctly handles wide characters (emojis) by creating continuation cells.

func (c *Canvas) WriteANSI(x, y int, text string) int
    WriteANSI renders ANSI-formatted text starting at (x, y), preserving inline
    colors and styles from SGR escape sequences. Returns the number of columns
    consumed. Clips at canvas right edge and bottom.

func (c *Canvas) WriteDefault(x, y int, text string, style Style) int
    WriteDefault is Write for normal text over a default surface: the style's
    BG is dropped so every cell inherits the surface below (a parent's
    PaintSurface, or the widget's own PaintDefaultSurface when standalone).
    Selected or highlighted text should keep its BG and use Write.

type Cell struct {
	Text         string
	Style        Style
	Continuation bool
	// Claim marks the cell as foreground-owned even when it is blank and has
	// the default style. This is useful for widgets whose layout owns a cell
	// without relying on text or style inference.
	Claim bool
	// Surface marks an explicit background painted by PaintSurface. Surface
	// cells remain eligible for decoration while their background is inherited
	// by later foreground writes.
	Surface bool
}
    Cell is a single terminal cell with printable content and visual style.
    Text should be a single printable character (or empty for a blank cell).
    Wide characters (emoji) occupy two consecutive cells; the right half should
    be stored as an empty Cell with the same style.

func ParseANSI(s string) []Cell
    ParseANSI decodes an ANSI-formatted string into a slice of Cells.
    By default, it uses the optimized zero-allocation ParseANSINew.
    If LOOM_FAST_ANSI is set to "0", "false", or "off", it falls back to
    ParseANSIOld.

func ParseANSINew(s string) []Cell
    ParseANSINew is the optimized ANSI parser that performs cluster collection
    and cell mapping with continuation cells for wide characters.

func ParseANSIOld(s string) []Cell
    ParseANSIOld is the legacy ANSI parser preserved for comparison and testing.

type Center = AlignBox
    Center is a convenience type for an AlignBox configured to center its child.

type Chart struct {
	Series []ChartSeries
	Mode   ChartMode
	Min    float64
	Max    float64
	// RangeSet fixes the vertical range to Min..Max; otherwise data is scaled.
	RangeSet bool
}
    Chart draws multiple numeric series with compact labeled axes.

func (*Chart) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult

func (*Chart) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult

func (*Chart) ContentHeight() int

func (*Chart) ContentWidth() int

func (ch *Chart) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the chart clipped to r. It is safe for small or empty regions.

func (ch *Chart) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure returns the preferred size at the given width: a plot of
    chartPlotHeight lines plus the axis and label lines, and a legend line when
    the chart has more than one series. Draw still fills any height it gets.

type ChartMode uint8
    ChartMode selects line or grouped-bar rendering.

const (
	ChartLine ChartMode = iota
	ChartGroupedBar
)
type ChartSeries struct {
	Name   string
	Values []float64
	Color  Color
}
    ChartSeries is one named numeric series. Values are plotted in input order.

type Choice struct {
	Items []Item
	Style ChoiceStyle
	// Fuzzy enables subsequence matching and score-ranked results.
	Fuzzy bool
	// ScrollbarMode overrides the spec default for this widget.
	ScrollbarMode ScrollbarMode
	Prompt        string // default "> "

	PromptTop bool            // place prompt on first row instead of last row
	OnSelect  func(item Item) // called on Enter or an activating click; if nil, Enter quits
	// SelectOnlyOnClick keeps a single click from confirming; Enter still invokes OnSelect.
	SelectOnlyOnClick bool
	// DoubleClickToActivate makes a matching second click activate the selected
	// item. The first click only selects; a double-click can activate even when
	// SelectOnlyOnClick is set.
	DoubleClickToActivate bool
	// MouseTextOnly restricts mouse selection and activation to rendered item content.
	MouseTextOnly bool

	// Input customization
	CursorAlign string // "start" or "end", default "start"
	Placeholder string // dim hint after the prompt while the query is empty; "" disables
	Controls    string // right-aligned controls/status label
	MaxWidth    int    // max width limit

	// MultiSelect turns the list into a checkbox picker: Space (or left-click)
	// toggles the item under the caret, Enter confirms the whole set, Esc aborts.
	// Checks are keyed by Item.Name so they survive filtering.
	MultiSelect bool

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Choice is a filterable, keyboard-navigable list of Items. Arrow keys move
    the selection; printable characters narrow the filter; Enter confirms; Esc
    or Ctrl-C aborts. Typing ':' or '/' activates command mode (see loom.Cmd,
    loom.Nav).

func NewChoice(items []Item) *Choice
    NewChoice creates a ready-to-use Choice with default style.

func (c *Choice) Aborted() bool
    Aborted reports whether the user dismissed without selecting.

func (c *Choice) AddCmd(cmd Cmd)
    AddCmd registers a view-local command accessible via ':name' in this widget.

func (c *Choice) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the Choice style from the theme.

func (c *Choice) Checked() []Item
    Checked returns the checked items in original list order (MultiSelect mode).
    It returns nil when the user aborted (Esc) so a cancelled picker yields no
    set.

func (c *Choice) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey drives navigation and filtering. ':' or '/' activates command
    mode; all other keys behave normally when inactive.

func (c *Choice) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse updates selection on hover or wheel, confirms on left-click,
    and jumps the viewport when the scrollbar track is clicked. e.Y is a
    widget-local 0-based row; viewOffset maps that back to a filtered index
    (mirrors Draw's fi mapping) so hit-tests stay correct once the list has been
    scrolled.

func (c *Choice) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for this choice widget.

func (c *Choice) Draw(cv *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the choice list into r. PromptTop=false (default): items fill
    the top, prompt occupies the last row. PromptTop=true: prompt occupies the
    first row, items fill the rest. When items exceed the visible area a scroll
    indicator appears on the right edge.

func (c *Choice) FilteredItem(i int) Item
    FilteredItem returns the item at index i in the current filtered list.
    Returns a zero Item if i is out of range.

func (c *Choice) FilteredSel() int
    FilteredSel returns the index of the current selection within the filtered
    list.

func (c *Choice) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether this widget is focused.

func (c *Choice) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget exposes the choice's command help popup, when open.

func (c *Choice) Nav() Nav
    Nav returns the navigation signal set by a prompt command (:home). NavNone
    means the user made a normal selection or cancelled.

func (c *Choice) Query() string
    Query returns the current filter query string.

func (c *Choice) SearchBar() *SearchBar
    SearchBar returns the underlying SearchBar component.

func (c *Choice) SelectIndex(i int)
    SelectIndex sets the selection to index i if in range.

func (c *Choice) Selected() (Item, bool)
    Selected returns the chosen Item and whether a selection was made (not
    aborted).

func (c *Choice) SetFocus(f bool)
    SetFocus sets the focus state of this widget.

func (c *Choice) SetItems(items []Item)
    SetItems replaces the item list, clears the filter query, and resets
    selection.

type ChoiceDefaults struct {
	DefaultPlaceholder string `yaml:"default_placeholder"`
	SelectionMarker    string `yaml:"selection_marker"`
	UnselectedMarker   string `yaml:"unselected_marker"`
	CheckedMarker      string `yaml:"checked_marker"`
	UncheckedMarker    string `yaml:"unchecked_marker"`
}
    ChoiceDefaults defines specced defaults for Choice.

type ChoiceStyle struct {
	Normal      Style
	Selected    Style
	Match       Style // style for matched runes; zero uses the row style with bold and underline enabled
	Prompt      Style
	Placeholder Style
	Scrollbar   ScrollbarStyle
	// Deprecated: Choice draws no border and ignores Border. Frame a Choice
	// with Box or Frame instead; the field stays for source compatibility.
	Border    Style
	SearchBar SearchBarStyle
}
    ChoiceStyle controls the visual appearance of a Choice widget.

func DefaultChoiceStyle() ChoiceStyle
    DefaultChoiceStyle returns styles derived from the specced default theme.

type ClockDefaults struct {
	Start string `yaml:"start"`
	Stop  string `yaml:"stop"`
	Reset string `yaml:"reset"`
}
    ClockDefaults defines the labels for timer and stopwatch controls.

type CloseDecision int
    CloseDecision is the answer of OnCloseRequest.

const (
	// CloseAllow lets the pane close. It is the zero value.
	CloseAllow CloseDecision = iota
	// CloseVeto keeps the pane running.
	CloseVeto
)
type CloseReason int
    CloseReason tells OnCloseRequest why the pane wants to close.

const (
	// CloseReasonQuitKey is a quit key from the spec (Ctrl-Q, F10) or Esc when
	// EscapeQuits is enabled.
	CloseReasonQuitKey CloseReason = iota
	// CloseReasonInterrupt is Ctrl-C or an interrupt, hangup or termination signal.
	CloseReasonInterrupt
)
type Cmd struct {
	Name  string       // command name, e.g. "help", "back", "home"
	Title string       // dim hint shown in the prompt: ":h[elp]  <Title>"
	Keys  []string     // optional direct key bindings (reserved for future use)
	Fn    func() error // nil for built-in commands
}
    Cmd is a command reachable from any widget's prompt by typing `:name` or
    `/name`.

type Color struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Color is a terminal color: reset, 256-color index, or 24-bit RGB.

func ColorIndex(n uint8) Color
    ColorIndex returns a 256-color palette entry (0–255).

func ColorRGB(r, g, b uint8) Color
    ColorRGB returns a 24-bit true-color value.

func ColorReset() Color
    ColorReset is the default terminal foreground or background color.

func (c Color) RGB() (r, g, b uint8, ok bool)
    RGB returns an approximate 24-bit value for c and whether one could be
    resolved. colorReset has no fixed RGB value (terminal-defined) and returns
    ok=false. Indexed colors are approximated using the standard xterm 256
    palette (6x6x6 color cube and grayscale ramp; 0-15 use common ANSI RGB
    values).

type ColorPicker struct {
	FG, BG     Color
	Target     ColorPickerTarget
	Selected   int
	Palette    []Color
	Style      Style
	FocusStyle Style
	OnChange   func(ColorPickerTarget, Color)
	OnClose    func()

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ColorPicker selects a foreground or background color and previews the pair.

func NewColorPicker(fg, bg Color) *ColorPicker
    NewColorPicker creates a picker initialized with foreground and background
    colors.

func (p *ColorPicker) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the normal and focused styles from a host theme.

func (p *ColorPicker) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey handles palette navigation, mode changes and completion.

func (p *ColorPicker) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse selects a swatch or toggles modes on right-click.

func (p *ColorPicker) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders contiguous color samples, a focus marker and preview.

func (p *ColorPicker) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether this picker owns keyboard focus.

func (p *ColorPicker) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure reports the one-row palette and its optional preview.

func (p *ColorPicker) PreviewStyle() Style
    PreviewStyle returns the selected foreground and background as one style.

func (p *ColorPicker) SetFocus(focused bool)
    SetFocus updates keyboard focus rendering.

type Confirm struct {
	Prompt string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Confirm is a yes/no prompt for preview→confirm flows (e.g. the final step
    of :git commit) and destructive-action guards. ←/→ (or h/l) move between
    Yes and No, 'y'/'n' answer directly, Enter confirms the highlighted choice,
    and Esc answers No. After the widget quits, Answered reports that a choice
    was made and Confirmed reports whether it was Yes.

func NewConfirm(prompt string) *Confirm
    NewConfirm creates a Confirm with the given prompt. The Yes option is
    highlighted by default; set DefaultNo to start on No for destructive
    actions.

func (c *Confirm) Answered() bool
    Answered reports whether the user made a choice (vs. the widget never ran).

func (c *Confirm) Confirmed() bool
    Confirmed reports whether the user chose Yes.

func (c *Confirm) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey drives the selection and answers the prompt.

func (c *Confirm) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse is a no-op; Confirm is keyboard-driven.

func (c *Confirm) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight reports the rows needed: prompt + options.

func (c *Confirm) DefaultNo() *Confirm
    DefaultNo starts the prompt highlighting No (safer for destructive actions).

func (c *Confirm) Draw(cv *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the prompt on the first row and the Yes/No options below,
    with the highlighted option marked and bold.

type ContentHeighter interface {
	ContentHeight() int
}
    ContentHeighter is an optional interface for widgets that can estimate their
    content height.

type ContentWidther interface {
	ContentWidth() int
}
    ContentWidther estimates preferred width from visible widget content.

type CursorHint struct {
	DX, DY   int

    CursorHint describes a cell's offset from the current mouse position.
    DX and DY are cell coordinates minus cursor coordinates.

type Dialog struct {
	Title   string
	Body    string
	Buttons []string
	Rect    Rect // explicit top-left and optional size; zero W/H are content-sized
	Width   int  // used when Rect is unset; zero sizes from content
	Height  int
	Style   Style
	Open    bool
	// Modeless embeds the prompt as ordinary content without capturing input
	// outside its allocation. NewDialog remains modal by default.
	Modeless bool
	OnSelect func(string)

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Dialog is a centered or positioned modal prompt rendered with Popup's border
    and background treatment. Enter selects the highlighted button and closes;
    without buttons it does nothing. Escape closes without calling OnSelect.
    Closing consumes the event without quitting or completing the hosting pane.

func NewDialog(title, body string, buttons ...string) *Dialog
    NewDialog creates an open modal dialog. The first button is highlighted.

func (d *Dialog) Activate()
    Activate reopens the dialog when its hosting tab is selected.

func (d *Dialog) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates dialog chrome and its modal popup.

func (d *Dialog) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey consumes closing actions and changes to the button selection.
    Unused keys and navigation with fewer than two buttons bubble to the parent.
    Tab is left to the container, which uses it to move focus between widgets.

func (d *Dialog) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult

func (d *Dialog) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)

func (d *Dialog) Measure(int) measure.Size
    Measure returns the dialog's outer size, including its border, so a fitted
    Grid row shows the body and buttons. The width argument is not used.

func (d *Dialog) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget captures mouse input exclusively while the dialog is open.

func (d *Dialog) SelectedButton() string
    SelectedButton reports the highlighted button label, or an empty string.

type Directory struct {
	Path    string
	Entries []FileEntry
}
    Directory is a filesystem directory and its entries.

func ReadDirectory(path string, opts DirectoryOptions) (Directory, error)
    ReadDirectory reads path without following symlinks merely to classify
    entries.

func (d Directory) EntryMap() map[string]FileEntry
    EntryMap maps raw entry names to their entries.

func (d Directory) EntryPath(name string) string
    EntryPath resolves a child name relative to the directory.

func (d Directory) Parent() (string, bool)
    Parent returns the parent directory and reports false at a volume root.

type DirectoryOptions struct {
	IncludeParent bool
}
    DirectoryOptions controls which navigation entries ReadDirectory returns.

type DividerStyle struct {
	Glyph string
	Style Style
}
    DividerStyle controls the glyph and appearance of a Split divider.

type DocState int
    DocState is the save state of a RichTextEdit document.

const (
	// DocStateUntitled means the document has no file path and no changes.
	DocStateUntitled DocState = iota
	// DocStateSaved means the document matches its file.
	DocStateSaved
	// DocStateModified means the document has unsaved changes.
	DocStateModified
	// DocStateError means the last save failed.
	DocStateError
)
func (s DocState) Label() string
    Label returns the spec-defined display label for the state.

type DoubleClickRecognizer struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    DoubleClickRecognizer recognizes two presses on the same target and button
    within the specced time and movement thresholds. Call Handle for each mouse
    event, including releases and motion, with the identity of the item under
    the pointer. An empty target clears a pending click.

func NewDoubleClickRecognizer(now func() time.Time) *DoubleClickRecognizer
    NewDoubleClickRecognizer creates a recognizer. Pass a clock for
    deterministic tests; nil uses the current wall clock.

func (r *DoubleClickRecognizer) Handle(e MouseEvent, target string) bool
    Handle consumes an input event for target and reports whether it completed a
    double-click. Only presses with a real button and non-empty target can start
    or complete a click pair.

type DurationFormatter func(time.Duration) string
    DurationFormatter formats the remaining or elapsed duration shown by a Timer
    or Stopwatch. A nil formatter uses mm:ss, growing to h:mm:ss as needed.

type EditorConfig struct {
	Theme     string `yaml:"theme" json:"theme"`
	MouseGrab bool   `yaml:"mousegrab" json:"mousegrab"`
	AltScreen bool   `yaml:"altscreen" json:"altscreen"`
}
    EditorConfig holds preferences loaded from editor.yaml or spec defaults.

func LoadEditorConfig(path string) (EditorConfig, error)
    LoadEditorConfig loads, parses, and validates editor preferences. If path is
    empty, DefaultEditorConfigPath() is checked. Missing default path returns
    spec defaults.

type EditorStatusIcons struct {
	Theme    string `yaml:"theme"`
	MouseOn  string `yaml:"mouse_on"`
	MouseOff string `yaml:"mouse_off"`
	AltOn    string `yaml:"alt_on"`
	AltOff   string `yaml:"alt_off"`

}
    EditorStatusIcons defines compact editor status caps and their colors.

type EventConsumer interface {
	ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
}
    EventConsumer processes key events and reports consumption and quit status.

type EventResult struct {
	Consumed bool
	Quit     bool
	Done     bool // the widget interaction is complete; the host app remains active
}
    EventResult indicates whether an input event (keyboard or mouse) was
    consumed, whether a widget interaction completed, and whether the
    application event loop should terminate. EventResult is a small value struct
    and must always be returned by value (not pointer).

func Consumed() EventResult
    Consumed returns an EventResult indicating that the event was consumed
    without quitting.

func DispatchKeyEvent(root Widget, ke KeyEvent) EventResult
    DispatchKeyEvent dispatches a key event to a widget.

func DispatchMouseEvent(root Widget, me MouseEvent) EventResult
    DispatchMouseEvent dispatches a mouse event to a widget.

func DispatchPasteEvent(root any, event PasteEvent) EventResult
    DispatchPasteEvent sends a paste only to widgets that explicitly support it.

func DoneResult() EventResult
    DoneResult returns an EventResult indicating that the widget interaction is
    complete, without requesting the host application's event loop to terminate.

func Handled() EventResult
    Handled returns an EventResult indicating that the event was consumed
    without quitting.

func Ignored() EventResult
    Ignored returns an EventResult indicating that the event was not consumed
    and does not request quit.

func Quit() EventResult
    Quit returns an EventResult indicating that the event was consumed and
    requests application termination.

func QuitResult() EventResult
    QuitResult returns an EventResult indicating that the event was consumed and
    requests application termination.

func Unhandled() EventResult
    Unhandled returns an EventResult indicating that the event was not handled.

type FileEntry struct {
	Name     string
	Path     string
	Kind     FileKind
	IsParent bool
}
    FileEntry describes one entry in a Directory.

func (e FileEntry) DisplayName() string
    DisplayName returns the entry name escaped for safe terminal display.

type FileKind uint8
    FileKind identifies the filesystem kind reported by a directory entry.

const (
	// FileKindRegular is a regular file.
	FileKindRegular FileKind = iota
	// FileKindDirectory is a directory.
	FileKindDirectory
	// FileKindSymlink is a symbolic link. Its target is not followed while reading.
	FileKindSymlink
	// FileKindSpecial is any other filesystem object.
	FileKindSpecial
)
type FileOpener struct {
	GOOS  string
	Start CommandStarter
}
    FileOpener launches files using the desktop opener for its platform.
    Start and GOOS may be supplied by callers to make launching deterministic in
    tests.

func (o FileOpener) Open(path string) error
    Open launches path, falling back to another platform opener only when a
    candidate executable is unavailable.

type FilePicker struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    FilePicker is a keyboard and mouse navigable filesystem picker.

func NewFilePicker(dir string, options FilePickerOptions) (*FilePicker, error)
    NewFilePicker reads dir and creates a reusable file or directory picker.

func (p *FilePicker) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the embedded list style.

func (p *FilePicker) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey navigates, selects, or cancels the picker.

func (p *FilePicker) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse forwards child-local coordinates to the embedded Choice.

func (p *FilePicker) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight reports the picker content height for a Viewport host.

func (p *FilePicker) Directory() Directory
    Directory returns the directory currently being browsed.

func (p *FilePicker) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the current path and entry list.

func (p *FilePicker) Entries() []FileEntry
    Entries returns the selectable or navigable entries currently shown.

func (p *FilePicker) FileName() string
    FileName returns the destination name entered in save mode.

func (p *FilePicker) List() *Choice
    List returns the underlying Choice for host customization.

func (p *FilePicker) Reset()
    Reset resets the done state so the file picker can be reused.

func (p *FilePicker) Selected() (FileEntry, bool)
    Selected returns the current directory entry, if one is selected.

type FilePickerMode uint8
    FilePickerMode controls which entries a FilePicker can select.

const (
	// FilePickerFiles selects regular files and uses directories for navigation.
	FilePickerFiles FilePickerMode = iota
	// FilePickerDirectories selects directories and hides files.
	FilePickerDirectories
	// FilePickerSave selects a file name in the current directory as a save destination.
	FilePickerSave
)
type FilePickerOptions struct {
	Mode FilePickerMode
	// FileName seeds the destination name in save mode.
	FileName string
	// FocusFileName starts save mode with the destination name field focused.
	FocusFileName bool
	// Patterns are filepath.Match globs applied to file names; directories are never filtered.
	Patterns []string
	Style    ChoiceStyle
	OnSelect func(path string)
	OnCancel func()
	// OnSave validates or writes a save-mode destination. An error keeps the
	// picker open so the caller can report the problem and the user can retry.
	OnSave func(path string) error
}
    FilePickerOptions configures a filesystem picker.

type FocusContainer interface {
	Focusable
	FocusNext() bool
	FocusPrevious() bool
}
    FocusContainer is a focusable composite that can move focus within itself.
    FocusNext and FocusPrevious return false when focus is already at the
    corresponding boundary, allowing a parent container to continue traversal.

type Focusable interface {
	Widget
	Focused() bool
	SetFocus(bool)
}
    Focusable is an optional interface for widgets that track input focus. Pane
    uses it to highlight the active widget when multiple widgets are present.

type Form struct {
	// AdvanceOnEnter moves from a single-line text field to the next field or action.
	// The final field retains the normal validation and submission behavior.
	AdvanceOnEnter bool
	Fields         []FormField
	Actions        []FormAction
	OnSubmit       func(map[string]any)
	OnCancel       func()
	Validation     map[int]string

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Form arranges input fields, validates them, and submits their current
    values.

func NewForm(fields []FormField) *Form
    NewForm constructs a form with the first field focused.

func (f *Form) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey routes editing keys and form navigation.

func (f *Form) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult

func (f *Form) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders an error summary followed by aligned field labels, editors,
    help, and actions.

func (f *Form) FocusIndex() int
    FocusIndex returns the index of the focused field, or the action index after
    the fields.

func (f *Form) FocusNext() bool

func (f *Form) FocusPrevious() bool

func (f *Form) Focused() bool

func (f *Form) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget returns the last visible modal in a form field.

func (f *Form) SetFocus(v bool)

type FormAction struct {
	Label      string
	Cancel     bool
	OnActivate func()
}
    FormAction is an action in the form's footer. Cancel actions invoke
    OnCancel.

type FormField struct {
	Label    string
	Widget   any // commonly TextInput (which needs a focused Draw argument), NumberInput, Toggle, or Choice
	Help     string
	Validate func() error
	Required bool
}
    FormField binds a label and optional validation to an existing input widget.

type Frame struct {
	Title            string        `yaml:"title"`
	Status           string        `yaml:"status"`
	Gap              int           `yaml:"gap"`
	Breakpoint       int           `yaml:"breakpoint"`
	Boxes            []Box         `yaml:"boxes"`
	Actions          []FrameAction `yaml:"actions"`
	Style            FrameStyle    `yaml:"-"`
	ControlSeparator string        `yaml:"control_separator"`
	FocusNextKey     string        `yaml:"focus_next_key"` // default: tab
	FocusPrevKey     string        `yaml:"focus_prev_key"` // default: shift-tab

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Frame places ordered boxes between title/status lines. A positive Breakpoint
    switches the row to a vertical stack at narrower widths; zero keeps a row.

func (f *Frame) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme restyles the frame and box chrome and forwards the theme to all
    box children that implement Themeable.

func (f *Frame) Box(id string) *Box
    Box returns a pointer to the box with matching ID, or nil if not found.

func (f *Frame) ConsumeKey(k KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey offers the event to the focused child before frame bindings.

func (f *Frame) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse focuses clicked boxes and forwards events inside a child's
    bounds.

func (f *Frame) ConsumePaste(e PasteEvent) EventResult

func (f *Frame) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight includes two chrome rows and the tallest box.

func (f *Frame) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw reserves the first and last rows for chrome. At one row only title
    fits.

func (f *Frame) FocusNext() bool
    FocusNext advances within the focused child, then to the next visible box.
    It returns false at the final descendant so a parent can continue traversal.

func (f *Frame) FocusPrevious() bool
    FocusPrevious retreats within the focused child, then to the previous
    visible box. It returns false at the first descendant.

func (f *Frame) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the frame is active. A root frame is active by
    default; SetFocus controls this state when the frame is nested.

func (f *Frame) FocusedBox() *Box
    FocusedBox returns the visible box receiving keyboard input, or nil.

func (f *Frame) HeightForWidth(width int) int
    HeightForWidth reports the preferred height, including chrome and stack
    gaps. It is independent of Draw, so resize never changes application data.

func (f *Frame) Layout(width, height int) []Rect
    Layout returns one bounded outer rectangle per declared box. Chrome takes
    precedence, then boxes in declaration order. Unavailable boxes have zero
    rectangles; areas too small for a full border are omitted rather than
    broken.

func (f *Frame) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget returns the last drawn modal in a visible frame box.

func (f *Frame) PaneRequest() (request PaneRequest)
    PaneRequest merges the terminal requirements of all boxes.

func (f *Frame) SetFocus(focused bool)
    SetFocus activates or deactivates this frame and its focused descendant.

func (f *Frame) StatusText() string
    StatusText derives current hints from visibility without mutating the spec.

func (f *Frame) Tick(now time.Time)

func (f *Frame) TickInterval() (shortest time.Duration)

type FrameAction struct {
	ID         string `yaml:"id"`
	Action     string `yaml:"action"`
	Key        string `yaml:"key"`
	Target     string `yaml:"target"`
	Hint       string `yaml:"hint"`
	HiddenHint string `yaml:"hidden_hint"`
	TitleHint  string `yaml:"title_hint"`
}
    FrameAction declares a bounded toggle or quit binding and its displayed
    hints. Toggle targets are box IDs; hints remain reachable even when all
    boxes hide.

type FrameStyle struct {
	Background Style
	Title      Style
	Status     Style
}
    FrameStyle controls the frame background, title, and status row.

type Gauge struct {
	Store  *MetricStore
	Metric string
	// Name is accepted as a readable alias for Metric.
	Name  string
	Value float64
	Min   float64
	Max   float64
	Width int
	// Options supplies all graph bar options. Width, Min, and Max fields on
	// Gauge override the corresponding options when set.
	Options graph.BarOptions
}
    Gauge renders the latest value from a metric store as a graph bar. When
    Store and Metric are unset, Value is rendered directly. Width is the number
    of graph cells and does not include RenderBar's optional wrappers.

func NewGauge(store *MetricStore, metric string, options graph.BarOptions) *Gauge
    NewGauge creates a metric-bound gauge using the supplied store and series
    name. The returned value can be further configured before drawing.

func (*Gauge) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey makes Gauge a passive widget.

func (*Gauge) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse makes Gauge a passive widget.

func (*Gauge) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight reports the one row used by a gauge.

func (g *Gauge) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth reports the preferred width including RenderBar wrappers.

func (g *Gauge) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the gauge at the top-left of r and clips it to the allocated
    rectangle. It is safe to draw into a zero-sized rectangle.

type Grid struct {
	Cols        int
	Children    []Widget
	FocusBG     Color          // background color of the focused cell; zero = default
	BorderMode  GridBorderMode // none, inner, or full; zero value draws no border
	BorderStyle Style          // border appearance; zero value uses the theme border
	FitRows     bool           // size each row to its tallest measured child
	OnSelect    func(i int)    // called on Enter if non-nil; prevents quit propagation

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Grid lays out widgets in a fixed number of columns. Row count is inferred
    from len(Children) and Cols. By default rows share the available height.
    With FitRows, each row uses the tallest child's Measurer height at its cell
    width, with a minimum of one line. Children without Measurer use one line.
    Spare height remains below the rows; overflow is clipped to the Grid area
    without scrolling. ChildRect reports the full layout bounds, including
    clipped portions. Borders occupy separate cells; a full border stays at the
    area's outside edge even when rows do not fill it. Navigation: Left/Right
    move within a row; Up/Down move between rows. OnSelect is called when Enter
    is pressed on a cell; if nil, Enter delegates to the focused child widget
    (which may return quit=true).

func NewGrid(cols int, children ...Widget) *Grid
    NewGrid creates a Grid with cols columns.

func (g *Grid) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the focus background color and forwards the theme to all
    children that implement Themeable.

func (g *Grid) ChildRect(i int) Rect
    ChildRect returns the drawn bounds of child i from the most recent Draw.

func (g *Grid) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey moves focus with arrow keys; Enter calls OnSelect or delegates to
    child.

func (g *Grid) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse routes to the child whose drawn cell contains the event.

func (g *Grid) ConsumePaste(e PasteEvent) EventResult

func (g *Grid) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for this grid layout.

func (g *Grid) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders all children into the grid within r. The focused cell receives
    a FocusBG background highlight before its child draws.

func (g *Grid) Focus() int
    Focus returns the index of the currently focused child.

func (g *Grid) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget returns the last visible active modal in the grid.

func (g *Grid) PaneRequest() (request PaneRequest)
    PaneRequest merges the terminal requirements of all children.

func (g *Grid) Tick(now time.Time)

func (g *Grid) TickInterval() (shortest time.Duration)

type GridBorderGlyphs struct {
	Horizontal  string `yaml:"horizontal"`
	Vertical    string `yaml:"vertical"`
	Cross       string `yaml:"cross"`
	TDown       string `yaml:"t_down"`
	TUp         string `yaml:"t_up"`
	TRight      string `yaml:"t_right"`
	TLeft       string `yaml:"t_left"`
	TopLeft     string `yaml:"top_left"`
	TopRight    string `yaml:"top_right"`
	BottomLeft  string `yaml:"bottom_left"`
	BottomRight string `yaml:"bottom_right"`
}
    GridBorderGlyphs contains the junction and line glyphs used by Grid borders.

type GridBorderMode string
    GridBorderMode controls whether Grid draws borders between cells and around
    its outside edge.

const (
	GridBorderNone  GridBorderMode = "none"
	GridBorderInner GridBorderMode = "inner"
	GridBorderFull  GridBorderMode = "full"
)
type HelpEntry struct {
	Keys  []string `yaml:"keys"`
	Cap   string   `yaml:"cap"`
	Ref   string   `yaml:"ref"`
	Label string   `yaml:"label"`
}
    HelpEntry is one row of a help section. Keys are bindings rendered
    with KeyCap; Cap overrides the rendered keycap text; Ref names a
    RichTextEditDefaults hotkey (e.g. "HotkeySave") whose binding and label fill
    the row.

type HelpSection struct {
	Title   string      `yaml:"title"`
	Entries []HelpEntry `yaml:"entries"`
}
    HelpSection is a titled group of help entries.

type HintBar struct {
	Entries []HintEntry
	Style   HintBarStyle
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    HintBar renders one row of atomic key/label pairs and runs actions on
    clicks. Mouse coordinates are zero-based and local to its last draw
    rectangle.

func NewEditorStatusBar(cfg EditorConfig) *HintBar
    NewEditorStatusBar creates compact, spec-defined theme, mouse capture and
    alternate-screen indicators. Theme detail drops first on narrow screens.

func NewHintBar(entries ...HintEntry) *HintBar
    NewHintBar creates a hint bar with the default theme's styles.

func (b *HintBar) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the cap and label colors from the theme.

func (b *HintBar) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey dispatches a binding to the same action used by mouse clicks.

func (b *HintBar) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse runs the cap or label's action on a left press; hover is inert.

func (b *HintBar) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth returns the display width needed to show every cap and detail.

func (b *HintBar) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw paints only complete caps and labels within the assigned first row.

func (b *HintBar) Text(width int) string
    Text returns the fitted pairs without ANSI styles or cap padding.

type HintBarStyle struct{ Cap, Label Style }
    HintBarStyle separates the bold key caps from the labels and row surface.

type HintEntry struct {
	Key, Label string
	// Binding is the decoded KeyEvent name, such as ctrl-s or f7.
	Binding string
	// Detail is optional context (for example a theme name), dropped before pairs.
	Detail string
	// DropPriority drops higher values first; ties drop from the end.
	DropPriority int
	Action       func() EventResult
}
    HintEntry pairs a display key and label with the action used by its binding.
    An empty Key is derived from Binding with KeyCap.

type ImageBackground struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ImageBackground renders an image as a dimmed Braille texture. It is safe to
    reuse across frames and resizes because the source image is immutable.

func LoadImageBackground(path string) (*ImageBackground, error)
    LoadImageBackground loads PNG or JPEG data from path and returns a terminal
    background. The image is fitted to the target rectangle while preserving its
    aspect ratio.

func (b *ImageBackground) DrawBackground(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    DrawBackground paints the image using the eight specced single-dot Braille
    glyphs. Each terminal cell represents a 2x4 sample block.

type InvalidationAware interface {
	SetInvalidate(func())
}
    InvalidationAware widgets accept a callback that requests a host redraw.
    The callback may be invoked from a background goroutine.

type Item struct {
	Name string
	Desc string
}
    Item is a named entry used by Choice and similar list widgets.

type KeyCapDefaults struct {
	Modifiers []KeyCapModifier `yaml:"modifiers"`
}
    KeyCapDefaults defines the modifier glyphs KeyCap renders, in display order.

type KeyCapModifier struct {
	Name  string `yaml:"name"`
	Glyph string `yaml:"glyph"`
}
    KeyCapModifier maps a binding modifier name (shift, ctrl, alt) to its glyph.

type KeyEvent struct {
	Key string // "up","down","left","right","home","end","delete","enter","esc",
	//            "backspace","tab","shift-tab","shift-up","shift-down","shift-left","shift-right",
	//            "ctrl-up","ctrl-down","ctrl-left","ctrl-right","alt-up","alt-down",
	//            "f1","f2","f3","f4","f5","f6","f7","f8","f9","f10","f11","f12",
	//            "ctrl-b","ctrl-c","ctrl-d","ctrl-f","ctrl-q","ctrl-u","ctrl-w",
	//            or "" for plain text
	Text string // typed printable text (Key == "" when Text != "")
}
    KeyEvent is a decoded keyboard event. Key names match common terminal
    conventions; Text carries printable input.

func DecodeKey(b []byte) KeyEvent
    DecodeKey converts raw bytes from a /dev/tty read into a KeyEvent.
    It handles both normal cursor keys (\x1b[A) and application cursor keys
    (\x1bOA) because ZSH ZLE enables DECCKM and zle -I does not reset it.
    See docs/TuiInput.md §3.

func (e KeyEvent) Is(keys ...string) bool
    Is reports whether the event name matches one of the provided key
    identifiers.

func (e KeyEvent) Name() string
    Name returns the special-key name or printable text carried by the event.

func (e KeyEvent) Rune() rune
    Rune returns the first printable rune in the event text, or zero otherwise.

type KeyHelp struct {
	KeyMap    *KeyMap
	Separator string
	Style     Style
}
    KeyHelp renders the labeled bindings in a KeyMap as one compact help line.
    The first configured key alias for each labeled action is shown.

func NewKeyHelp(km *KeyMap) *KeyHelp
    NewKeyHelp creates a compact key help widget for km.

func (h *KeyHelp) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme sets the help text and surface colors.

func (h *KeyHelp) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey does not consume keyboard events.

func (h *KeyHelp) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse does not consume mouse events.

func (h *KeyHelp) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders key help clipped to the supplied rectangle.

func (h *KeyHelp) Text() string
    Text returns the compact, deterministic key help line.

type KeyHelpRow struct {
	Header bool   // section title row
	Key    string // padded keycap column (empty for headers and wrapped continuations)
	Text   string // description, or the section title for headers
}
    KeyHelpRow is one rendered row of a sectioned key help table.

func KeyHelpSections(sections []HelpSection, width int) []KeyHelpRow
    KeyHelpSections lays out grouped help entries as a two-column table of
    the given width: section headers, an aligned keycap column and wrapped
    descriptions.

type KeyMap struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    KeyMap maps key names to logical action names.

    Key names are matched without regard to ASCII letter case. Non-ASCII key
    names are compared exactly.

func NewKeyMap(bindings map[string][]string) *KeyMap
    NewKeyMap creates a key map from action names to their key aliases.

func NewKeyMapWithLabels(bindings map[string][]string, labels map[string]string) *KeyMap
    NewKeyMapWithLabels creates a key map and assigns optional short help labels
    to actions. Bindings and labels are copied; later caller changes do not
    affect the map.

func (km *KeyMap) Action(e KeyEvent) string
    Action returns the action bound to e, or an empty string if none matches.
    If a key is bound to multiple actions, the lexicographically first action
    name is returned.

func (km *KeyMap) Label(action string) string
    Label returns the short help label for action, or an empty string when none
    was configured.

func (km *KeyMap) Matches(e KeyEvent, action string) bool
    Matches reports whether e is bound to action.
