type MetricPoint = MetricSample
    MetricPoint is an alias for MetricSample, useful when referring to a series
    as a sequence of points.

type MetricSample struct {
	Value float64
	At    time.Time
}
    MetricSample is one observation in a named metric series.

    Samples are kept in publish order. At is the timestamp supplied to Publish;
    it is not used to reorder observations.

type MetricSnapshot struct {
	Series map[string][]MetricSample
}
    MetricSnapshot is a detached view of all metric series at one instant.
    The map and all sample slices are copied from the store. Mutating them does
    not change the store or any other snapshot.

func (s MetricSnapshot) Clone() MetricSnapshot
    Clone returns an independent copy of the snapshot.

func (s MetricSnapshot) Get(name string) []MetricSample
    Get returns a copy of the named series. It returns nil when the series is
    not present.

func (s MetricSnapshot) Latest(name string) (MetricSample, bool)
    Latest returns the newest published sample for name.

func (s MetricSnapshot) Names() []string
    Names returns all series names in stable lexical order.

func (s MetricSnapshot) Values(name string) []float64
    Values returns the values in the named series, oldest first.

type MetricStore struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    MetricStore stores named rolling metric series. Publishing and snapshotting
    may safely happen concurrently from different goroutines.

func NewMetricStore(opts ...MetricStoreOption) *MetricStore
    NewMetricStore creates an empty, concurrency-safe metric store.

func (s *MetricStore) Get(name string) []MetricSample
    Get returns a detached copy of a named series from the current store state.

func (s *MetricStore) Latest(name string) (MetricSample, bool)
    Latest returns the newest published sample for name.

func (s *MetricStore) Names() []string
    Names returns all currently known series names in stable lexical order.

func (s *MetricStore) Publish(name string, value float64, at time.Time)
    Publish appends a sample to the named series. Empty names are ignored.
    When retention is configured, older samples are discarded independently for
    each series.

func (s *MetricStore) PublishNow(name string, value float64)
    PublishNow appends a sample using time.Now as its timestamp.

func (s *MetricStore) Snapshot() MetricSnapshot
    Snapshot returns a deeply detached view of every series. Later publishes do
    not alter the returned map or slices.

func (s *MetricStore) Values(name string) []float64
    Values returns the values in a named series from the current store state.

type MetricStoreOption func(*metricStoreConfig)
    MetricStoreOption configures a MetricStore.

func Capacity(capacity int) MetricStoreOption
    Capacity is an alias for Retention for callers that describe the option in
    terms of the backing ring capacity.

func Retention(capacity int) MetricStoreOption
    Retention limits each named series to the newest capacity samples.
    A non-positive capacity leaves series unbounded.

func WithRetention(capacity int) MetricStoreOption
    WithRetention is an explicit alias for Retention.

type ModalMouseCapture struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ModalMouseCapture routes events before ordinary hit-testing or focus
    changes. Its zero value is ready to use. Hosts and containers retain one
    instance across events so a modal press owns its drag/release even after
    dismissing the modal.

func (c *ModalMouseCapture) Dispatch(root Widget, e MouseEvent) (result EventResult, captured bool)
    Dispatch returns captured=true whenever the modal layer owns the event.
    It preserves Done and Quit and always marks a captured event Consumed, even
    when the modal's handler ignores it. Coordinates reaching the target are
    0-based and target-local; a backdrop event may have negative coordinates.

type ModalMouseProvider interface {
	ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
}
    ModalMouseProvider exposes the topmost active modal mouse recipient. The
    rectangle's origin is relative to the provider's allocation, not the canvas;
    events outside that rectangle still belong exclusively to the modal. Return
    nil when no modal is active. A modal may return itself with a zero origin.

type MouseAction int
    MouseAction classifies a mouse event.

const (
	MousePress      MouseAction = iota
	MouseRelease                // button released
	MouseHover                  // motion with no button held
	MouseDrag                   // motion with button held
	MouseScrollUp               // wheel up
	MouseScrollDown             // wheel down
)
type MouseButton int
    MouseButton identifies which button triggered the event.

const (
	MouseLeft   MouseButton = iota // left / primary
	MouseMiddle                    // middle / scroll-click
	MouseRight                     // right / secondary
	MouseNone                      // hover or scroll (no button)
)
type MouseConsumer interface {
	ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
}
    MouseConsumer processes mouse events and reports consumption and quit
    status.

type MouseDefaults struct {
	DoubleClickInterval time.Duration `yaml:"double_click_interval"`
	MovementTolerance   int           `yaml:"movement_tolerance"`
}
    MouseDefaults defines specced defaults for mouse gestures.

type MouseEvent struct {
	Action     MouseAction
	Button     MouseButton
	Shift      bool // SGR modifier bit 4.
	Alt        bool // SGR modifier bit 8.
	Ctrl       bool // SGR modifier bit 16.
	X, Y       int  // DecodeMouse reports 1-based terminal coordinates; Pane converts them before widget dispatch.
	RawX, RawY int  // Original 1-based SGR coordinates, preserved when Pane translates X/Y.
}
    MouseEvent is a decoded SGR (1006) mouse report.

type Nav int
    Nav is a navigation signal propagated from a widget through the caller
    chain.

const (
	NavNone Nav = iota // normal exit: selection made or user cancelled
	NavHome            // user invoked :home — unwind to the application root
)
type Notif struct {
	Message string
	Style   Style
	Timeout time.Duration
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Notif renders a single-line status message at the bottom of its Rect. After
    Timeout the message is hidden on the next Draw call (timeout of 0 means the
    message persists until explicitly cleared).

func (n *Notif) Clear()
    Clear removes the current message immediately.

func (n *Notif) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey is a no-op; Notif does not consume keyboard events.

func (n *Notif) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse is a no-op; Notif does not consume mouse events.

func (n *Notif) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the message on the last row of r if visible.

func (n *Notif) Show(msg string)
    Show sets a new message and starts the timeout clock.

type NumberInput struct {
	Value  *float64
	Min    float64
	Max    float64
	Step   float64
	Format string
	// FixedWidth pads the complete control to a stable display width. Zero keeps the natural width.
	FixedWidth int
	// Align controls value alignment inside FixedWidth; the default is left.
	Align Align

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    NumberInput edits a bounded floating-point value. Left and right step the
    value; Enter starts inline editing, Enter commits, and Esc cancels.

func NewNumberInput(value *float64, min, max float64) *NumberInput
    NewNumberInput creates a bounded numeric input. A zero Step defaults to 1.

func (n *NumberInput) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey steps, edits, commits, or cancels the value.

func (n *NumberInput) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse handles mouse scroll wheel and click stepping.

func (n *NumberInput) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the current value, or the active editor when focused.

func (n *NumberInput) Editing() bool
    Editing reports whether inline editing is active.

func (n *NumberInput) Error() string
    Error returns validation feedback from the most recent failed commit.

func (n *NumberInput) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the numeric input owns focus.

func (n *NumberInput) SetFocus(f bool)
    SetFocus updates focus and cancels any active inline edit when focus is
    lost.

func (n *NumberInput) StepBy(direction float64)
    StepBy changes the value by direction times Step and clamps it to the
    bounds.

func (n *NumberInput) String() string
    String returns the formatted current value with step indicators.

type NumberInputDefaults struct {
	Step         float64 `yaml:"step"`
	LeftGlyph    string  `yaml:"left_glyph"`

	InvalidError string  `yaml:"invalid_error"`
	BelowMinFmt  string  `yaml:"below_min_fmt"`
	AboveMaxFmt  string  `yaml:"above_max_fmt"`
}
    NumberInputDefaults defines specced defaults for NumberInput.

type Orientation = StackDir
    Orientation is the axis on which a Split arranges its children. It aliases
    StackDir so Horizontal and Vertical are shared consistently by containers.

type Paginator struct {
	Page     int
	Pages    int
	Style    PaginatorStyle
	OnChange func(page int)

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Paginator provides page navigation and reports page changes to its host.
    Page is zero-based; Pages is clamped to at least one.

func NewPaginator(pages int) *Paginator
    NewPaginator creates a paginator with the requested number of pages.

func (p *Paginator) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey handles page up and page down without requesting application
    quit.

func (p *Paginator) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult

    and local to the widget rectangle.

func (p *Paginator) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the page indicators from the top-left of r.

    PaginatorStyle selects the page indicator presentation.

const (
	PaginatorDots PaginatorStyle = iota
	PaginatorNumeric
)
type PaintCanvas struct {
	// Smoothing is the maximum stroke simplification distance in braille dots.
	// Zero preserves the original lines. Closed rectangular strokes retain corners.
	Smoothing int
	// Controls shows a Tune button and enables T to cycle the specced tolerances.
	Controls bool

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    PaintCanvas is a mouse-driven drawing area. Each terminal cell holds up to
    eight painted dots using the Unicode braille pattern block.

func (p *PaintCanvas) Clear()
    Clear removes all painted dots and ends the current stroke.

func (p *PaintCanvas) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey clears the drawing when the user presses c or Ctrl-L.

func (p *PaintCanvas) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse starts a stroke on left press, connects drag points with
    Bresenham lines, and ends the stroke on left release.

func (p *PaintCanvas) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders painted dots into r, clipped to the widget's available area.

type PaintCanvasDefaults struct {
	TuneLabel       string `yaml:"tune_label"`
	SmoothingLabel  string `yaml:"smoothing_label"`
	SmoothingLevels []int  `yaml:"smoothing_levels"`
}
    PaintCanvasDefaults defines stroke tuning controls.

type Pane struct {
	MaxCols int // canvas width cap; 0 = use terminal width

	// DebugMode overlays a 1-cell ruler around the pane and insets widget bounds by 1 cell.
	DebugMode bool

	Resizeable bool

	// InlineOnly opts out of the automatic switch to the alternate screen: the
	// pane stays inline even when it is nearly as big as the terminal. Loom's
	// normal mode is to switch when the dimensions get resize-error prone.
	InlineOnly bool

	// DisableDefaultQuit suppresses the fallback exit behavior for unhandled
	// quit keys (spec quit_keys), Ctrl-C and, when enabled, Esc.
	DisableDefaultQuit bool
	// DisableGlobalF10Quit lets a pane keep F10 within its widget tree.
	// The default is to quit before dispatching F10 to any widget.
	DisableGlobalF10Quit bool
	// EscapeQuits makes an unhandled Esc close the app. Esc never quits by
	// default (spec escape_quits); overlays and widgets consume it first.
	EscapeQuits bool
	// KittyKeyboard opts in to the kitty keyboard protocol (progressive
	// enhancement flag 1, "disambiguate escape codes") while Run is active, so
	// Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+I and friends arrive as distinct CSI-u keys.
	// Loom pushes the flag on start and pops it on close, panic exit and around
	// Suspend. Terminals without support ignore it. Spec: pane.kitty_keyboard.
	KittyKeyboard bool
	// OnCloseRequest, when non-nil, is asked before the pane closes because of
	// a quit key or an interrupt/termination signal. Returning CloseVeto keeps
	// the loop running; the app may call Quit later (e.g. after a dialog).
	OnCloseRequest func(reason CloseReason) CloseDecision

	// Background is composited after the root widget on every frame.
	Background Background
	// BackgroundOnRedraw disables independent animation ticks for animated
	// backgrounds. The background still renders whenever the pane redraws.
	// The zero value keeps animated backgrounds updating continuously.
	BackgroundOnRedraw bool
	// ReduceMotion disables animated background ticks while retaining its static
	// rendering on normal foreground redraws.
	ReduceMotion bool
	// Metrics, when non-nil, receives rolling redraw measurements.
	Metrics *RenderMetrics
	// ResizeConfig controls runtime resize rendering behaviors.
	ResizeConfig ResizeConfig

	// WidthGuardDuration configures the burst timeout before restoring full width.
	// When 0, defaults to 1 second.
	WidthGuardDuration time.Duration

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Pane manages an inline terminal region and drives the widget event loop.

func New(height int) (*Pane, error)
    New opens /dev/tty, enters raw mode, and reserves height rows below the
    current cursor position. Call Close (or defer it) to restore the terminal.

    Always uses /dev/tty — never os.Stdin — so the pane works inside shells
    and command substitution (e.g. `foo=$(bar)`), where stdin may be a pipe.
    See docs/TuiInput.md §1.

func (p *Pane) AutoFullscreenReasons() (byWidth, byHeight bool)
    AutoFullscreenReasons reports which detectors (width, height) currently ask
    for the full-screen layout. Both are false when detection is off or the pane
    is InlineOnly. It is for status displays; the pane acts on it by itself.

func (p *Pane) Close()
    Close tears down the pane: clears the reserved region, restores terminal
    state, and closes /dev/tty. Safe to call multiple times.

func (p *Pane) DisableMouse()
    DisableMouse sets the base mode to native terminal text selection.
    Interactive overlays temporarily retain click tracking until the last
    overlay closes. Call before Run or from an event handler. EnableMouse
    re-enables tracking.

func (p *Pane) EffectiveGuardN() int
    EffectiveGuardN is the guard width in force: the width latched at the last
    SIGWINCH when adaptive mode is enabled and measurable, otherwise the manual
    WidthGuardN.

func (p *Pane) EnableCursorEffects()
    EnableCursorEffects enables all currently implemented cursor effects.

func (p *Pane) EnableCursorPressPulse()
    EnableCursorPressPulse enables the one-shot expanding effect for key and
    button presses at the latest known pointer position.

func (p *Pane) EnableCursorProximity()
    EnableCursorProximity enables spec-driven cursor hints and background
    brightening. It also enables any-motion reports and must be called before
    Run.

func (p *Pane) EnableCursorStarTrail()
    EnableCursorStarTrail enables the spec-driven trailing star effect. It also
    enables cursor proximity and any-motion mouse reports.

func (p *Pane) EnableMouse()
    EnableMouse turns on SGR mouse tracking (button press, release, hover,
    scroll). Call before Run or from an event handler. Mouse events reach the
    root Widget's ConsumeMouse method.

func (p *Pane) EnableMouseClicks()
    EnableMouseClicks tracks clicks and wheel events without any-motion reports.
    Call before Run or from an event handler; Close restores normal mouse
    behavior.

func (p *Pane) Invalidate()
    Invalidate requests a repaint. It is safe to call from any goroutine and
    never blocks.

func (p *Pane) Post(fn func())
    Post queues fn to run on the event-loop goroutine before the next frame,
    then requests a repaint. It is safe to call from any goroutine, never blocks
    on the loop and never drops callbacks; queued callbacks run in FIFO order
    and a burst is drawn once. Callbacks posted before Run start on its first
    loop turn. Post after Close is a no-op.

func (p *Pane) Quit()
    Quit asks Run to return at the next loop turn. It is safe to call from
    widget callbacks and from other goroutines, and bypasses OnCloseRequest.

func (p *Pane) ResetResizeModes()
    ResetResizeModes restores the Pane's ResizeConfig to spec defaults.

func (p *Pane) ResetTicker()
    ResetTicker postpones the next ticker update by its current interval.
    It is safe to call from widget callbacks, including callbacks on another
    goroutine.

func (p *Pane) Resize(newHeight int)
    Resize adjusts the pane height dynamically. If the height increases and
    overflows the terminal screen, it scrolls the terminal up to reserve the
    required space. If it decreases, it clears the abandoned lines.

func (p *Pane) Run(root Widget) error
    Run renders root on every frame and dispatches events until the root signals
    quit or an unrecoverable error occurs.

func (p *Pane) RunStartup(ctx context.Context, cfg StartupConfig) error
    RunStartup starts a splash controller, renders it until its completion hold
    has elapsed, and then hands the pane to the destination widget. It returns
    when the destination quits, the context is cancelled, or a transition or
    pane error occurs. The completed splash frame is always drawn once before
    handover; no caller-side sleep is needed.

func (p *Pane) RunWatch(ctx context.Context, root Widget, cadence Cadence, collect func(time.Time) error) error
    RunWatch runs collection and redraw on independent timers. Collection and
    widget callbacks share the event-loop goroutine; Draw must not collect data.
    The caller owns Close, as with Run. Collection callbacks must not block.

func (p *Pane) Screen() ScreenMode
    Screen reports the layout currently in force, including an automatic
    promotion to full screen.

func (p *Pane) SetMaxCols(maxCols int)
    SetMaxCols sets the canvas width cap. A value of zero keeps the full
    terminal width, even when the widget requests a narrower default.

func (p *Pane) SetResizeMode(id string, val bool) bool
    SetResizeMode updates a mode on the Pane's ResizeConfig.

func (p *Pane) SetScreenMode(m ScreenMode)
    SetScreenMode selects the layout by setting the resize modes it consists of.
    The next frame performs the switch. Auto full screen, when enabled,
    can still promote an inline pane; disable it in ResizeConfig to force
    ScreenInline.

func (p *Pane) SetWidthGuardN(n int)
    SetWidthGuardN updates the number of columns deducted during an active
    resize burst.

func (p *Pane) Suspend(fn func() error) (err error)
    Suspend hands the terminal to fn, typically to run an interactive child
    process such as $EDITOR on the same tty, and takes it back afterwards.
    Call it from the event loop (a key or mouse handler, or a Post callback).

    Before fn runs, Suspend stops the input reader (unread input stays queued
    for the child; bytes the pane already read are replayed after resume),
    leaves the alternate screen, disables mouse tracking, bracketed paste and
    the kitty keyboard protocol, shows the cursor and restores the terminal mode
    the pane started from (cooked). After fn returns, it re-enters raw mode,
    restores the screen, mouse and paste modes, re-reads the terminal size,
    restarts the reader and repaints every row. An inline pane reserves its rows
    again below the cursor the child left. Resizes during fn are applied once
    on resume, and an interrupt (Ctrl-C) that reached the pane while fn ran is
    dropped, since it was meant for the child.

    The terminal is restored even if fn returns an error or panics; the panic
    is re-raised after the restore. Suspend returns fn's error, or the error of
    restoring raw mode.

func (p *Pane) ToggleResizeMode(id string) bool
    ToggleResizeMode inverts a mode on the Pane's ResizeConfig.

func (p *Pane) WidthGuardActive() bool
    WidthGuardActive reports whether the pane is currently within an active
    SIGWINCH burst and rendering with the width guard deduction applied.

func (p *Pane) WinchRate() float64
    WinchRate returns the measured SIGWINCH rate in events per second.

type PaneDefaults struct {
	MaxCols       int           `yaml:"max_cols"`
	EscKeyTimeout time.Duration `yaml:"esc_key_timeout"`
	GuardDuration time.Duration `yaml:"guard_duration"`
	ViewPanStep   int           `yaml:"view_pan_step"`
	KittyKeyboard bool          `yaml:"kitty_keyboard"`
}
    PaneDefaults defines specced defaults for Pane.

type PaneRequest struct {
	Mouse      int
	Resizeable bool
	MaxCols    int
	OwnsQuit   bool
}
    PaneRequest declares terminal capabilities a widget needs from its host
    before the pane starts processing input. Zero values request no special
    capability; Mouse is a terminal mouse mode (1000 for clicks or 1003 for all
    tracking), and MaxCols 0 means unbounded.

type PaneRequester interface {
	PaneRequest() PaneRequest
}
    PaneRequester optionally lets a widget declare terminal capabilities to its
    host pane. Pane reads the request once before starting its event loop.

type Paneable interface {
	Widget
	ContentHeighter
	// Selected returns the chosen Item and whether a selection was made.
	Selected() (Item, bool)
	// Nav returns the navigation signal set by a prompt command (e.g. :home).
	// NavNone means the user made a normal selection or cancelled.
	Nav() Nav
}
    Paneable is a Widget that can be driven by RunPane: it reports the height
    it wants (ContentHeight), the user's choice (Selected), and any navigation
    signal raised from its command prompt (Nav). Choice and Table implement it.

type PasteConsumer interface {
	ConsumePaste(PasteEvent) EventResult
}
    PasteConsumer optionally handles a complete terminal paste event.

type PasteEvent struct{ Text string }
    PasteEvent carries the text from one bracketed terminal paste operation.

type PillCluster struct {
	Pills []ProviderPill
	Gap   int          // spacing between pills; defaults to 2
	Align layout.Align // horizontal alignment within available width; default AlignCenter
}
    PillCluster is a widget that renders a horizontal row of ProviderPills.

    NewPillCluster creates a new PillCluster with default gap and centered
    alignment.

func (pc *PillCluster) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey implements Widget.

func (pc *PillCluster) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse implements Widget.

func (pc *PillCluster) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight is 1 for a single-row cluster.

func (pc *PillCluster) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth computes the total horizontal column width of the pill cluster.

func (pc *PillCluster) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)

type Popup struct {
	Title  string
	Inner  Widget
	Open   bool
	Width  int // 0 = half the canvas width
	Height int // 0 = half the canvas height
	Style  Style
	// Modeless embeds popup chrome as ordinary content without capturing input
	// outside its allocation. Nested modal overlays still acquire capture.
	Modeless bool
	// DismissOnOutsideClick closes the popup after a left click outside its border.
	// NewPopup enables this by default.
	DismissOnOutsideClick bool

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Popup overlays a fixed-size inner Widget centered over the pane. While Open,
    it captures all keyboard and mouse events before the background widget.
    Set Open=false to dismiss.

func NewPopup(title string, inner Widget) *Popup
    NewPopup creates a Popup wrapping inner with the given title.

func (p *Popup) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates popup chrome and forwards the theme to its inner widget.

func (p *Popup) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey forwards to Inner while Open; Esc closes the popup.

func (p *Popup) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse forwards to Inner while Open and consumes all backdrop events.

func (p *Popup) ConsumePaste(e PasteEvent) EventResult

func (p *Popup) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for this popup.

func (p *Popup) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the popup centered in r, with a simple box border. If not Open,
    Draw does nothing.

func (p *Popup) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget captures mouse input exclusively while the popup is open.

type ProgressBar struct {
	// Options configures glyphs, brackets and width. Width zero uses the
	// specced default. Pattern and ANSI are ignored: Done manages the
	// pattern and Style provides colors.
	Options graph.BracketedBarOptions
	// DonePattern replaces the bar after Done. Empty uses the specced default.
	DonePattern string
	// Style is applied to the whole bar, brackets included.
	Style Style
	// Align positions the bar horizontally inside its rect.
	Align layout.Align
	// Indeterminate animates a one-third-width pulse when enabled.
	Indeterminate bool
	// ShowPercent appends a percentage label.
	ShowPercent bool
	// ShowCount appends the current value and total, followed by Unit.
	ShowCount bool
	// Unit labels the values in the count label.
	Unit string
	// StyleFill and StyleEmpty style filled and empty cells independently.
	StyleFill  Style
	StyleEmpty Style
	// Interval controls indeterminate animation cadence. Zero uses the default.
	Interval time.Duration
	// Total is the determinate maximum. Zero uses 100 for compatibility.
	Total float64

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ProgressBar is a determinate bracketed progress bar. Producers drive it by
    calling Set (or passing bar.Set as a progress callback), from any goroutine.
    Set requests a host redraw only when the visible bar changes, so high-rate
    callbacks cost one comparison each. Done swaps the bar to a repeating
    pattern (default ":"), the same completion look as SplashView.

func NewProgressBar() *ProgressBar
    NewProgressBar returns an empty bar with specced defaults and sub-character
    fill.

func (p *ProgressBar) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme implements Themeable.

func (p *ProgressBar) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey implements Widget; the bar takes no input.

func (p *ProgressBar) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse implements Widget; the bar takes no input.

func (p *ProgressBar) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight implements ContentHeighter.

func (p *ProgressBar) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth implements ContentWidther.

func (p *ProgressBar) Done()
    Done marks the bar complete and shows the done pattern.

func (p *ProgressBar) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw implements Widget.

func (p *ProgressBar) IsDone() bool
    IsDone reports whether Done was called since the last Reset.

func (p *ProgressBar) Reset()
    Reset clears the value and the done state.

func (p *ProgressBar) Set(value float64)
    Set updates the value (0 to 100, clamped). It requests a redraw only when
    the number of visible fill subunits changes.

func (p *ProgressBar) SetInvalidate(fn func())
    SetInvalidate implements InvalidationAware.

func (p *ProgressBar) SetResetTick(fn func())
    SetResetTick implements TickerControlAware.

func (p *ProgressBar) Tick(time.Time)
    Tick advances the marquee pulse and requests a redraw.

func (p *ProgressBar) TickInterval() time.Duration
    TickInterval implements Ticker. Determinate bars do not request ticks.

func (p *ProgressBar) Value() float64
    Value returns the last value passed to Set.

type ProgressBarDefaults struct {
	Width        int           `yaml:"width"`
	DonePattern  string        `yaml:"done_pattern"`
	DemoInterval time.Duration `yaml:"demo_interval"`
	DemoStep     float64       `yaml:"demo_step"`
}
    ProgressBarDefaults defines specced defaults for the ProgressBar widget.

type ProviderPill struct {
	Name   string
	Symbol string
	State  ProviderState
}
    ProviderPill represents a single provider status indicator badge.

func (p ProviderPill) PlainText() string
    PlainText returns the unstyled string representation: "<Symbol> <Name>".

func (p ProviderPill) Width() int
    Width returns the display column width of the pill.

type ProviderState int
    ProviderState represents the lifecycle status of an external provider.

const (
	// ProviderPending indicates a provider awaiting initialization.
	ProviderPending ProviderState = iota
	// ProviderFetching indicates a provider currently being queried.
	ProviderFetching
	// ProviderDone indicates successful provider initialization.
	ProviderDone
	// ProviderFailed indicates provider error or timeout.
	ProviderFailed
	// ProviderSkipped indicates provider initialization was bypassed.
	ProviderSkipped
)
type ProviderTask struct {
	Name     string
	Symbol   string
	Duration time.Duration // simulated duration if Action is nil
	Action   func(ctx context.Context) error
}
    ProviderTask defines an initialization task for a provider.

type RawScreen struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    RawScreen is the "final render loop" for a persistent, full-screen redraw
    loop (a `--watch`-style command redrawing in place on an interval, like
    `watch(1)` or htop) whose content needs inline per-cell ANSI color/style
    that a loom.View would strip (View collapses every line to a single Style;
    see view.go). Renderers like graph.RenderTreemap must never embed
    terminal-state control sequences themselves -- only content and SGR
    color/style codes -- and RawScreen is where that terminal safety belongs
    instead: it is the one place responsible for keeping the terminal clean and
    capping over-wide content, so every raw-ANSI redraw loop gets it for free
    instead of re-deriving it.

    RawScreen always draws relative to the physical top-left of the terminal
    (row 1), taking over the full visible screen on every Draw -- the same
    convention `watch(1)`/htop use. That is deliberately NOT anchored to
    wherever the cursor happened to be when Open was called (contrast with Pane,
    which reserves a fixed region below the shell cursor and anchors all
    its drawing there -- see pane.go's startRow). Do not use RawScreen for a
    one-shot "print once and exit" path: it WILL overwrite existing terminal
    content above the current line, since positioning to row 1 has no idea
    what was there before -- use WriteRows for that instead. This was a real
    regression caught by PTY-testing the treemap example: routing its plain
    (non-watch) print through RawScreen clobbered prior shell prompt lines that
    should have stayed in scrollback.

    Concretely, RawScreen guarantees two things no matter what its caller's rows
    contain:

     1. No row ever reaches the terminal wider than the terminal's live column
        count. A too-wide row is silently clipped (ClipRow), not left to the
        terminal's own auto-wrap -- auto-wrap is additionally disabled as a
        second line of defense, but clipping is authoritative. Wrapping is what
        turns one bad row into a cascading, whole-screen scramble: the wrapped
        remainder eats the start of the next row's line, and an explicit newline
        then advances *again*, so every following row lands one line further out
        of place.
     2. Every row is positioned with an absolute cursor move rather than drawn
        via sequential newlines, so a bad or stale row can only corrupt its own
        line -- the next row still lands exactly where it belongs, and any error
        self-heals on the very next Draw instead of accumulating.

    On a non-terminal out (redirected/piped stdout), Draw writes rows as plain
    newline-separated lines, uncapped -- there is no PTY to auto-wrap against,
    and a piped consumer may legitimately want the untruncated content.

func OpenRawScreen(out *os.File) *RawScreen
    OpenRawScreen prepares out for a sequence of Draw calls: hides the cursor
    and disables terminal auto-wrap (DECAWM) when out is a real terminal.
    Both are restored by Close. Safe to use on a non-terminal out.

func (s *RawScreen) Close() error
    Close restores auto-wrap and cursor visibility. Safe to call multiple times,
    and a no-op on a non-terminal out.

func (s *RawScreen) Draw(rows []string) error
    Draw renders one frame: rows[i] is drawn at terminal row i+1. See the
    RawScreen doc comment for the two safety guarantees this provides on a real
    terminal. Terminal width is re-queried on every call so a resize between
    frames is honored immediately.

type Rect struct {
	X, Y int // top-left corner
	W, H int // width and height
}
    Rect describes a rectangular region within the canvas (0-based, top-left
    origin).

func (r Rect) Contains(x, y int) bool
    Contains reports whether (x, y) falls inside r.

type RenderMetrics struct {
	LoomFPS        float64
	AstraFPS       float64
	AstraTargetFPS float64
	RedrawTime     time.Duration
	DrawTime       time.Duration // clear + widget draw (last frame)
	BackgroundTime time.Duration // background composition (last frame)
	FlushTime      time.Duration // building and writing the frame to the terminal (last frame)
	RedrawAvg      time.Duration
	RedrawMax      time.Duration
	BytesPerFrame  int

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    RenderMetrics reports recent completed redraw performance. RedrawTime and
    the phase times are the last frame; the Avg and Max fields and BytesPerFrame
    cover the last completed one-second window, which makes them steadier for
    comparing features.

type ResizeConfig struct {
	Coalesce           bool
	AtomicFlush        bool
	RowClear           bool
	SynchronizedOutput bool
	AutoWrap           bool
	OutOfBandClear     bool
	FullScreenBuffer   bool
	ResizeHandling     bool
	WidthGuard         bool
	WidthGuardN        int
	AdaptiveGuard      bool
	AltScreen          bool

	// Quasi-fullscreen detection, see QuasiFullscreen.
	AutoFullscreen bool // switch to the full-screen layout when the pane is nearly full height
	FullByWidth    bool // detect by width
	FullByHeight   bool // detect by height
	FullMarginCols int  // full when terminal cols - wanted cols <= this
	FullMarginRows int  // full when terminal rows - wanted rows <= this
	FullMinPercent int  // also full at this percent of the terminal height; 0 = off
	FullLeakGuard  bool // re-assert auto-wrap and clear pane rows around alt-screen switches
	FullAlt        bool // use the alternate screen for the automatic full-screen layout
}
    ResizeConfig holds the active boolean flags controlling resize and flush
    behaviors.

func DefaultResizeConfig() ResizeConfig
    DefaultResizeConfig returns a ResizeConfig populated with the spec-defined
    defaults.

func (c *ResizeConfig) Get(id string) (bool, bool)
    Get returns the state of the named mode, and true if the mode identifier
    exists.

func (c *ResizeConfig) IsDiagnosticOnly(id string) bool
    IsDiagnosticOnly reports whether a mode is designated for diagnostic
    comparison only.

func (c ResizeConfig) QuasiFullscreen(wantCols, wantRows, termCols, termRows int) bool
    QuasiFullscreen reports whether a pane that wants wantCols x wantRows on
    a termCols x termRows terminal should be shown as a full screen. Width
    and height are checked separately (FullByWidth, FullByHeight) and either
    one is enough. Width is full within FullMarginCols of the terminal width,
    where wantCols <= 0 means "no cap", i.e. the whole width. Height is full
    within FullMarginRows of the terminal height, or at least FullMinPercent
    percent of it. It is pure so the policy can be unit-tested.

func (c *ResizeConfig) Reset()
    Reset restores all modes to their spec-defined defaults.

func (c *ResizeConfig) Set(id string, val bool) bool
    Set updates the state of the named mode, returning true if the mode
    identifier was valid.

func (c *ResizeConfig) Toggle(id string) bool
    Toggle inverts the named mode, returning true if the mode identifier was
    valid.

type ResizeModeSpec struct {
	ID             string `yaml:"-"`
	Title          string `yaml:"title"`
	Description    string `yaml:"description"`
	Default        bool   `yaml:"default"`
	DiagnosticOnly bool   `yaml:"diagnostic_only"`
	Key            string `yaml:"key"`
	GuardN         int    `yaml:"guard_n,omitempty"`
	// Adaptive guard policy (see WinchMeter); only set on adaptive_guard.
	WindowMS int `yaml:"window_ms,omitempty"`
	MinN     int `yaml:"min_n,omitempty"`
	MaxN     int `yaml:"max_n,omitempty"`
	RateStep int `yaml:"rate_step,omitempty"`
}
    ResizeModeSpec defines the metadata and default configuration for a single
    resize mode.

type ResizeModesSpec struct {
	ModeOrder      []string                  `yaml:"mode_order"`
	Modes          map[string]ResizeModeSpec `yaml:"modes"`
	AutoFullscreen AutoFullscreenSpec        `yaml:"auto_fullscreen"`
}
    ResizeModesSpec holds all resize modes declared in spec/resize.yaml.

type RichDocument struct {
	Lines []RichLine
}
    RichDocument is a flow-based document. Lines preserve empty lines, including
    a final empty line after a trailing newline.

func ParseMarkup(src string) (*RichDocument, error)
    ParseMarkup parses .tui bracket markup into a RichDocument. Parsing is
    strict: unknown attributes, malformed or mismatched tags and tags left
    open at the end of a line return a *MarkupError. CRLF and CR become LF,
    and one trailing newline is dropped, as in FromANSI. Image tags render their
    alt text; use ParseMarkupWith to render images.

func ParseMarkupWith(src string, opts MarkupOptions) (*RichDocument, error)
    ParseMarkupWith is ParseMarkup with options for image tags.

func (d *RichDocument) FromANSI(input string)
    FromANSI replaces d with the styled text represented by an ANSI SGR stream.
    Non-SGR escape sequences are consumed and never interpreted as terminal
    commands. CRLF and bare CR line endings are normalized to LF.

func (d RichDocument) ToANSI() string
    ToANSI serializes visible text and SGR styling, ending with a full reset.
    Pill labels are serialized as text; semantic metadata remains in the
    document.

func (d RichDocument) ToMarkup() string
    ToMarkup serializes d as .tui bracket markup. Each styled span becomes one
    [attrs]text[/] group; default-styled text stays bare. The result ends with a
    newline, which ParseMarkup drops again. Pill, link and code metadata are not
    part of the v1 format; their visible text is kept.

func (d RichDocument) ToPlainText() string
    ToPlainText returns visible text, with logical lines joined by LF.

type RichLine struct {
	Spans []RichSpan
}
    RichLine is an ordered sequence of styled spans on one logical line.

type RichPill struct {
	Kind     string
	ID       string
	Metadata map[string]string
}
    RichPill stores application-defined data for an atomic inline token.

type RichPosition struct {
	Line   int
	Offset int
}
    RichPosition identifies a rune offset in a logical rich document line.

type RichSpan struct {
	Text     string
	Style    Style
	PillData *RichPill
	Link     string
	Code     bool
}
    RichSpan is text with a visual style and optional semantic metadata.
    PillData marks an atomic token; its Text is the label shown to the user.

type RichTextEdit struct {
	Document       *RichDocument
	Cursor         RichPosition
	SelectionFrom  RichPosition
	SelectionTo    RichPosition
	HasSelection   bool
	SelectionStyle Style
	// Highlights are display-only ranges, independent of editing selection.
	Highlights  []RichTextHighlight
	ActiveStyle Style
	ScrollX     int
	ScrollY     int
	ShowCursor  bool
	ShowPopover bool
	// PopoverDefaults configures popup behavior; initialized from the embedded spec.
	PopoverDefaults RichTextEditDefaults

	// ViewMode makes the editor read-only: navigation, selection and copy work;
	// every edit, style key and the format popover are disabled and edit keys
	// return Ignored so the app can use them.
	ViewMode bool
	// BoxMode draws box glyphs into adjacent document cells with arrow keys.
	BoxMode bool
	// GhostCursorEnabled allows vertical and horizontal navigation into empty
	// document space. The default comes from spec/defaults.yaml.
	GhostCursorEnabled bool
	// ShowFileBar reserves the final row for the File menu and document status.
	// It is disabled by default to preserve the viewport.
	ShowFileBar bool
	// FilePath is the path associated with the document by SaveAs or Save.
	FilePath string
	// LastSaveError holds the most recent save failure, including an error
	// returned after choosing a destination in the asynchronous save picker.
	LastSaveError error
	// OnStateChange, when set, is called once per DocState transition, after
	// the key, mouse event or save that caused it.
	OnStateChange func(state DocState)
	// OnOpenRequest, when set, is called when the user asks to open a file
	// (Open menu item or its hotkey). The host decides how to present files.
	OnOpenRequest func()
	// OnCloseRequest, when set, is called when the user asks to close the
	// document (Close menu item or its hotkey). The host runs its unsaved-changes
	// guard and then calls Close. Without it, RequestClose calls Close directly.
	OnCloseRequest func()
	// SerializeDocument optionally serializes the document for saving. A nil
	// callback uses RichDocument.ToANSI.
	SerializeDocument func(*RichDocument) ([]byte, error)

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    RichTextEdit edits a RichDocument with styled spans, selection, and a
    scrolling viewport.

func NewRichTextEdit(doc *RichDocument) *RichTextEdit
    NewRichTextEdit creates a rich text view for doc. A nil document is treated
    as an empty document.

func NewRichTextEditFromFile(path string) (*RichTextEdit, error)
    NewRichTextEditFromFile creates a RichTextEdit populated with content from
    path. A .tui path is parsed as bracket markup and saved with ToMarkup;
    a markup syntax error is returned with the path, line and column. Other
    paths use ANSI. If path does not exist, it initializes an empty document
    bound to path. It sets FilePath = path and ShowFileBar = true. Markup image
    tags show their alt text; use NewRichTextEditFromFileWith to render images.

func NewRichTextEditFromFileWith(path string, opts MarkupOptions) (*RichTextEdit, error)
    NewRichTextEditFromFileWith is NewRichTextEditFromFile with options for
    parsing a .tui file, such as media.MarkupOptions(path) to render images.
    Saving writes rendered images as styled cells, not as image tags.

func NewRichTextView(doc *RichDocument) *RichTextEdit
    NewRichTextView creates a read-only RichTextEdit for doc (ViewMode,
    no popover).

func (e *RichTextEdit) AddHelpSection(section HelpSection)
    AddHelpSection appends a host-specific section to the F1 help, after the
    built-in sections.

func (e *RichTextEdit) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the editor's file menu, status and hotkey chrome.

func (e *RichTextEdit) ClearSelection()
    ClearSelection removes the current selection.

func (e *RichTextEdit) Close()
    Close discards the document and its file association and leaves an empty,
    untitled buffer. It does not ask about unsaved changes; hosts do that first.

func (e *RichTextEdit) ConsumeKey(key KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey applies navigation, text editing, selection, and inline
    formatting. It fires OnStateChange when the key changed the document state.

func (e *RichTextEdit) ConsumeMouse(mouse MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse positions the cursor and supports click-drag selection.
    It fires OnStateChange when the event changed the document state.

func (e *RichTextEdit) CursorShape() CursorShape
    CursorShape reports the terminal cursor style required by the editor mode.

func (e *RichTextEdit) DocState() DocState
    DocState reports the single source of truth for the document's save state.
    A failed save wins over modified; unchanged documents without a path are
    untitled.

func (e *RichTextEdit) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders visible lines and styled spans, scrolls the cursor into view,
    paints selected text, and places the terminal cursor when focused.

func (e *RichTextEdit) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the editor currently has keyboard focus.

func (e *RichTextEdit) HotkeyBar() *HintBar
    HotkeyBar returns structured, clickable hints for the editor's key actions.
    Draw the bar in the host's hint row and route row-local mouse events to it.

func (e *RichTextEdit) HotkeyHint(width int) string
    HotkeyHint returns the most useful file and help shortcuts for the available
    width.

func (e *RichTextEdit) IsModified() bool
    IsModified reports whether the document has unsaved changes compared to its
    last saved state.

func (e *RichTextEdit) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget captures mouse input while an editor overlay is active.

func (e *RichTextEdit) ModalOpen() bool
    ModalOpen reports whether a popup, menu or visible format popover captures
    input. ModalMouseTarget exposes that state to hosts and containers.
    A toolbar appearing during document drag selection acquires capture after
    the release.

func (e *RichTextEdit) RequestClose()
    RequestClose asks to close the document. The host's OnCloseRequest owns the
    unsaved-changes guard; without one the document closes immediately.

func (e *RichTextEdit) RequestOpen()
    RequestOpen asks the host to open a file by calling OnOpenRequest.

func (e *RichTextEdit) Save() error
    Save writes the document to its associated path. If no path is associated,
    it opens a FilePicker in save mode and returns while the user chooses one.

func (e *RichTextEdit) SaveAs(path string) error
    SaveAs serializes the document, writes it to path, and associates path only
    after both serialization and writing succeed. Without SerializeDocument the
    format follows path: .tui writes markup, anything else ANSI, so Save As to
    another extension converts the document.

func (e *RichTextEdit) SetFocus(focused bool)
    SetFocus sets the editor focus state.

func (e *RichTextEdit) SetSelection(from, to RichPosition)
    SetSelection sets a half-open selection range in rune offsets.

	Bindings          map[string][]string `yaml:"bindings"`
	UndoLimit         int                 `yaml:"undo_limit"`
	MultiClickWindow  time.Duration       `yaml:"multi_click_window"`

	ShowPopover       bool                `yaml:"show_popover"`
	HelpTitle         string              `yaml:"help_title"`
	HelpMaxWidth      int                 `yaml:"help_max_width"`
	HelpMaxHeight     int                 `yaml:"help_max_height"`
	HelpPageStep      int                 `yaml:"help_page_step"`

	ViewLabel         string              `yaml:"view_label"`

	StatusSeparator   string              `yaml:"status_separator"`
	StatusTruncation  string              `yaml:"status_truncation"`
	PopoverMinWidth   int                 `yaml:"popover_min_width"`

	ActionClosesMenu          bool   `yaml:"action_closes_menu"`
	MenuFocusKey              string `yaml:"menu_focus_key"`
	ArrowsCancelUnfocusedMenu bool   `yaml:"arrows_cancel_unfocused_menu"`
	UnselectAfterAction       bool   `yaml:"unselect_after_action"`
	UnselectOnCancel          bool   `yaml:"unselect_on_cancel"`
	PopupOpenKey              string `yaml:"popup_open_key"`
	AutoPopupOnSelection      bool   `yaml:"auto_popup_on_selection"`
	PopupOpenDelayMS          int    `yaml:"popup_open_delay_ms"`
	CycleNavigation           bool   `yaml:"cycle_navigation"`
	PositionPreference        string `yaml:"position_preference"`
	DismissOnScroll           bool   `yaml:"dismiss_on_scroll"`
	MouseHoverFocus           bool   `yaml:"mouse_hover_focus"`

	SelectionBG           int           `yaml:"selection_bg"`
	ToolbarFG             int           `yaml:"toolbar_fg"`
	ToolbarBG             int           `yaml:"toolbar_bg"`
	SeparatorGlyph        string        `yaml:"separator_glyph"`
	SeparatorFG           int           `yaml:"separator_fg"`
	SeparatorBG           int           `yaml:"separator_bg"`
	PointerUpGlyph        string        `yaml:"pointer_up_glyph"`
	PointerDownGlyph      string        `yaml:"pointer_down_glyph"`
	PointerFG             int           `yaml:"pointer_fg"`
	BoxDrawLabel          string        `yaml:"box_draw_label"`
	PopoverLabels         []string      `yaml:"popover_labels"`
	BoxStyleLabels        []string      `yaml:"box_style_labels"`
	BoxStyleDefault       string        `yaml:"box_style_default"`
	GhostCursorEnabled    bool          `yaml:"ghost_cursor_enabled"`
	PopoverFocusFG        int           `yaml:"popover_focus_fg"`
	PopoverFocusBG        int           `yaml:"popover_focus_bg"`
	LinkFG                int           `yaml:"link_fg"`
	LinkUnderline         bool          `yaml:"link_underline"`
	SavePopupMaxWidth     int           `yaml:"save_popup_max_width"`
	SavePopupMaxHeight    int           `yaml:"save_popup_max_height"`
	StateUntitledLabel    string        `yaml:"state_untitled_label"`
	StateSavedLabel       string        `yaml:"state_saved_label"`
	StateModifiedLabel    string        `yaml:"state_modified_label"`
	StateErrorLabel       string        `yaml:"state_error_label"`
	FileMenuTitle         string        `yaml:"file_menu_title"`
	FileMenuMnemonic      string        `yaml:"file_menu_mnemonic"`
	HotkeyHelpBinding     string        `yaml:"hotkey_help_binding"`
	HotkeyHelpLabel       string        `yaml:"hotkey_help_label"`
	HotkeySaveBinding     string        `yaml:"hotkey_save_binding"`
	HotkeySaveLabel       string        `yaml:"hotkey_save_label"`

	HotkeyOpenLabel       string        `yaml:"hotkey_open_label"`

	HotkeyQuitBinding     string        `yaml:"hotkey_quit_binding"`
	HotkeyQuitLabel       string        `yaml:"hotkey_quit_label"`

}
    RichTextEditDefaults defines selection and popover presentation defaults.

type RichTextHighlight struct {
	From, To RichPosition
	Style    Style
}
    RichTextHighlight marks a half-open range in document rune coordinates.
    Style controls highlighted cells without changing saved content or
    selection.

type Router struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Router manages screen transitions between multiple views defined in the
    layout configuration.

func (r *Router) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey processes key events, returning quit=true on unhandled ESC.

func (r *Router) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse forwards mouse events to the active view.

func (r *Router) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for the active view, respecting
    view/app constraints.

func (r *Router) Current() string
    Current returns the name of the active view.

func (r *Router) Deeplink(path string) error
    Deeplink navigates through a colon-separated path of view names, pushing
    each onto the history so Esc/back returns through every step. Empty segments
    are skipped. It returns an error naming the offending segment (and listing
    the available views) when a segment does not match a known view.

    Example: "list:settings" lands on the settings view with [root, list] in
    history, so two Esc presses walk back to the root.

func (r *Router) Draw(c *Canvas, rect Rect)
    Draw renders the active view.

func (r *Router) GoBack() bool
    GoBack pops the last view from history and sets it active. Returns true if
    successful.

func (r *Router) RouteTo(name string)
    RouteTo switches the active view to name and adds current to history.

func (r *Router) ViewNames() []string
    ViewNames returns the names of all routable views, sorted for stable output.

type Row struct {
	Cells []string
	Key   string
}
    Row is a structured table entry. Cells maps column-by-index to display
    strings; Key is the unique identifier returned by Selected() as Item.Name.

type RowColumn struct {
	Width int    `yaml:"width"`
	Align string `yaml:"align"`
	Bold  bool   `yaml:"bold"`
}
    RowColumn reserves a fixed number of terminal cells for each value.

type Rows struct {
	Columns  []RowColumn `yaml:"columns"`
	Values   [][]string  `yaml:"values"`
	Gap      int         `yaml:"gap"`
	Ellipsis string      `yaml:"ellipsis"`
}
    Rows renders fixed-width, declared columns. Leftmost columns take priority
    when space is short; trailing columns are clipped or omitted. Values do not
    influence column positions. Ellipsis is supplied by the declaration.

func (*Rows) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey keeps static rows inert.

func (*Rows) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse keeps static rows inert.

func (rows *Rows) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight returns one line per declared value row.

func (rows *Rows) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth returns the declared columns and gaps' preferred cell width.

func (rows *Rows) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw clips all values to their column and the child's isolated canvas.

func (rows *Rows) GetValues() [][]string
    GetValues returns the active row values.

func (rows *Rows) SetValues(values [][]string)
    SetValues updates row values dynamically from Go application code.

type ScreenMode int
    ScreenMode is where the pane draws: a few rows below the prompt, the whole
    terminal, or the whole alternate screen.

const (
	ScreenInline ScreenMode = iota // reserved rows below the prompt
	ScreenFull                     // full terminal from row 1 on the primary screen
	ScreenAlt                      // full terminal on the alternate screen
)
type ScrollbarDefaults struct {
	Mode           ScrollbarMode `yaml:"mode"`
	ForegroundChar string        `yaml:"foreground_char"`
	BackgroundChar string        `yaml:"background_char"`
}
    ScrollbarDefaults defines scrollbar visibility and its one-cell glyphs.

type ScrollbarMode string
    ScrollbarMode controls when a widget displays its scrollbar.

const (
	// ScrollbarAuto displays a scrollbar only when content overflows.
	ScrollbarAuto ScrollbarMode = "auto"
	// ScrollbarAlways displays a scrollbar regardless of overflow.
	ScrollbarAlways ScrollbarMode = "always"
	// ScrollbarNever hides the scrollbar and does not reserve its column.
	ScrollbarNever ScrollbarMode = "never"
)
type ScrollbarStyle struct {
	Track Style
	Thumb Style
}
    ScrollbarStyle controls the visual appearance of scrollbar cells.

func DefaultScrollbarStyle() ScrollbarStyle
    DefaultScrollbarStyle returns terminal-default track and thumb styles.

type SearchBar struct {
	Prompt      string         // prompt prefix, default "> "
	Placeholder string         // dim hint shown when Query is empty; "" disables
	Query       string         // current typed filter text
	Controls    string         // right-aligned controls/status label
	Focused     bool           // whether search bar is focused (shows cursor)
	CursorAlign string         // "start" or "end", default "start"
	Style       SearchBarStyle // visual styling
	MaxWidth    int            // optional max render width

	OnChange func(query string) // called when Query changes
	OnSubmit func(query string) // called on Enter
	OnAbort  func()             // called on Esc / quit keys

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    SearchBar is a reusable search and filter input widget. It manages prompt
    rendering, query input, cursor positioning, placeholder hints, right-aligned
    controls, and command-mode (: / /) interactions.

func NewSearchBar() *SearchBar
    NewSearchBar creates a ready-to-use SearchBar with default style and prompt.

func (s *SearchBar) AddCmd(cmd Cmd)
    AddCmd registers a view-local command accessible via ':name' in this widget.

func (s *SearchBar) Clear()
    Clear resets the query string to empty.

func (s *SearchBar) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey processes keyboard events for SearchBar.

func (s *SearchBar) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse handles mouse interactions for SearchBar.

func (s *SearchBar) Draw(cv *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the search bar into region r.

func (s *SearchBar) IsCommandMode() bool
    IsCommandMode reports whether command mode is currently active.

func (s *SearchBar) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget exposes the search bar's command help popup, when open.

func (s *SearchBar) Nav() Nav
    Nav returns the navigation signal set by a prompt command (:home).

func (s *SearchBar) SetFocused(focused bool)
    SetFocused updates focus state.

func (s *SearchBar) SetQuery(q string)
    SetQuery sets the query string, updating state and firing OnChange if
    changed.

type SearchBarDefaults struct {
	Prompt      string `yaml:"prompt"`
	Placeholder string `yaml:"placeholder"`
}
    SearchBarDefaults defines specced defaults for the SearchBar widget.

type SearchBarStyle struct {
	Container   Style // full search bar container background and foreground
	Prompt      Style // prompt prefix (e.g. "> " or "⌕ ")
	Query       Style // typed query text
	Placeholder Style // hint shown when Query is empty
	Controls    Style // right-aligned controls/hints
}
    SearchBarStyle controls the visual appearance of a SearchBar widget.

func DefaultSearchBarStyle() SearchBarStyle
    DefaultSearchBarStyle returns styles derived from the specced default theme.

type Setting struct {
	Label   string
	Kind    SettingKind
	Bool    *bool    // KindBool: pointer to the governed value
	Str     *string  // KindString: pointer to the governed value
	Options []string // KindChoice: available values
	Index   *int     // KindChoice: pointer to the current index
	Num     *float64 // KindNumber: pointer to the governed value
	Min     float64  // KindNumber: inclusive lower bound
	Max     float64  // KindNumber: inclusive upper bound
	Step    float64  // KindNumber: step amount; zero defaults to 1
	Format  string   // KindNumber: fmt format; empty defaults to %g
}
    Setting is a single configurable option. Set the fields used by Kind: Bool,
    Str, Options+Index, or Num+Min+Max+Step.

type SettingKind int
    SettingKind identifies how a Setting is rendered and edited.

const (
	KindBool   SettingKind = iota // toggle: true / false
	KindString                    // editable text value
	KindChoice                    // cycle through a fixed list of options
	KindNumber                    // bounded numeric value
)
type Settings struct {
	Items  []Setting
	Prompt string // header line; empty = no header

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Settings is a navigable list of configurable options. ↑ ↓ move between
    settings; Enter / → toggle, advance or edit; ← steps a KindChoice or
    KindNumber backward. Esc returns quit=true.

    A KindString row enters inline edit mode on Enter/→: printable keys append,
    Backspace deletes, Enter commits, Esc cancels (restoring the prior value
    without quitting the widget). Navigation is locked while editing.

func NewSettings(items []Setting) *Settings
    NewSettings creates a Settings widget.

func (s *Settings) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey navigates settings and edits values.

func (s *Settings) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse is a no-op for now.

func (s *Settings) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for this settings list.

func (s *Settings) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders each setting as a labeled row with its current value. The
    selected row is bold; unselected rows are normal.

func (s *Settings) Editing() bool
    Editing reports whether a KindString row is currently being edited.

func (s *Settings) Sel() int
    Sel returns the index of the currently selected setting.

type Sparkline struct {
	Store  *MetricStore
	Metric string
	// Series is accepted as a readable alias for Metric.
	Series string
	Values []float64
	Width  int
	Min    float64
	Max    float64
	// Options supplies all graph sparkline options. Width, Min, and Max fields
	// on Sparkline override the corresponding options when set.
	Options graph.SparklineOptions
}
    Sparkline renders a metric history using graph.RenderSparkline. Metric and
    Store bind it to a named series; Values can be used for a direct series.
    Width is the number of graph cells.

func NewSparkline(store *MetricStore, metric string, options graph.SparklineOptions) *Sparkline
    NewSparkline creates a metric-bound sparkline using the supplied store and
    series name. The returned value can be further configured before drawing.

func (*Sparkline) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey makes Sparkline a passive widget.

func (*Sparkline) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse makes Sparkline a passive widget.

func (*Sparkline) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight reports the one row used by a sparkline.

func (s *Sparkline) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth reports the configured sparkline width.

func (s *Sparkline) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the sparkline at the top-left of r and clips it to the
    allocated rectangle.

type Spinner struct {
	Label    string

	// Has unexported fields.

func (s *Spinner) Stop()

type SplashConfig struct {
	Title        string
	Tasks        []ProviderTask
	TickInterval time.Duration // animation ticker rate; defaults to 80ms
	HoldDuration time.Duration // duration to hold completed state before transition; defaults to 400ms
}
    SplashConfig configures the SplashController.

type SplashController struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    SplashController coordinates the animation ticks, async provider tasks,
    and user skip/dismissal interactions for a startup splash screen.

func NewSplashController(cfg SplashConfig) *SplashController
    NewSplashController creates and initializes a SplashController.

func (sc *SplashController) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey intercepts navigation / dismissal keys (Esc, q, Enter, Ctrl-C).

func (sc *SplashController) Dismiss()
    Dismiss immediately stops tasks and transitions to dismissed state.

func (sc *SplashController) Done() <-chan struct{}
    Done returns a channel that is closed when tasks finish or splash is
    dismissed.

func (sc *SplashController) Snapshot() SplashSnapshot
    Snapshot returns a copy of the current state snapshot.

func (sc *SplashController) Start(ctx context.Context)
    Start begins the animation tick loop and async provider task execution.

type SplashDefaults struct {
	BracketWidth int           `yaml:"bracket_width"`
	PillGap      int           `yaml:"pill_gap"`
	FooterText   string        `yaml:"footer_text"`
	StepText     string        `yaml:"step_text"`
	TickInterval time.Duration `yaml:"tick_interval"`
	HoldDuration time.Duration `yaml:"hold_duration"`
}
    SplashDefaults defines specced defaults for splash lifecycle and widgets.

type SplashSnapshot struct {
	State        SplashState
	SpinnerFrame int
	Progress     float64 // 0.0 to 100.0
	StepText     string
	Pills        []ProviderPill
	Dismissed    bool
	Completed    bool
}
    SplashSnapshot captures an immutable state of the splash screen for
    rendering.

type SplashState int
    SplashState describes the lifecycle phase of the splash screen.

const (
	// SplashInitializing is the initial idle state before background tasks start.
	SplashInitializing SplashState = iota
	// SplashRunning is active while background provider tasks are in flight.
	SplashRunning
	// SplashCompleted indicates all tasks finished normally.
	SplashCompleted
	// SplashDismissed indicates the splash screen was dismissed or skipped by the user.
	SplashDismissed
)
type SplashView struct {
	Title        string
	SpinnerFrame int
	Progress     float64 // 0.0 to 100.0
	Pattern      string  // if set, overrides progress bar with repeating pattern (e.g. ":")
	StepText     string
	Pills        []ProviderPill
	FooterText   string // keyboard hint, e.g. "Esc to skip"
	BracketWidth int    // inner bar width, default 24 or 32
	PillGap      int    // spacing between pills, default 2
	Controller   *SplashController

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    SplashView is a declarative widget that renders a complete centered splash
    screen.

func NewSplashView(title string, pills ...ProviderPill) *SplashView
    NewSplashView creates a SplashView with default settings matching
    HarnezSplashTarget.

func (sv *SplashView) ApplySnapshot(snap SplashSnapshot)
    ApplySnapshot updates the view properties from a SplashSnapshot.

func (sv *SplashView) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey implements Widget.

func (sv *SplashView) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse implements Widget.

func (sv *SplashView) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight returns the fixed height required for the splash content
    block.

func (sv *SplashView) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth returns the preferred width (the widest sub-component).

func (sv *SplashView) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the splash screen centered horizontally and vertically inside
    r.

func (sv *SplashView) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure implements Measurer.

type Split struct {
	Orientation Orientation
	Ratio       float64
	Gap         int
	MinFirst    int
	MinSecond   int
	Divider     DividerStyle
	First       Widget
	Second      Widget

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Split lays out two widgets along one axis. Ratio is the preferred fraction
    assigned to First after Gap has been reserved. Minimums are measured on the
    split axis and are honored whenever the available space permits.

func NewSplit(first, second Widget) *Split
    NewSplit returns an evenly divided horizontal split with a one-cell divider.

func (s *Split) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey traverses children with Tab and Shift-Tab, then delegates other
    keys to the focused child.

func (s *Split) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse forwards an event to the child under the pointer, translating
    split-local coordinates to that child's local 0-based coordinates.

func (s *Split) ConsumePaste(e PasteEvent) EventResult

func (s *Split) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders both children and the divider in r.

func (s *Split) FocusNext() bool
    FocusNext moves to the next focusable descendant, returning false at the
    end.

func (s *Split) FocusPrevious() bool
    FocusPrevious moves to the previous focusable descendant, returning false at
    the start.

func (s *Split) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the split owns focus.

func (s *Split) Layout(r Rect) (Rect, Rect)
    Layout returns the child rectangles for bounds r. The space between them
    is the divider. When both minimums cannot fit, First is bounded first and
    Second receives the remainder.

func (s *Split) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget returns the topmost active modal in either split child.

func (s *Split) SetFocus(focused bool)
    SetFocus updates focus for the split and its selected descendant.

func (s *Split) SetRatio(ratio float64)
    SetRatio clamps and stores the preferred first-child ratio.

type SplitDefaults struct {
	VerticalDivider   string  `yaml:"vertical_divider"`
	HorizontalDivider string  `yaml:"horizontal_divider"`
	DefaultRatio      float64 `yaml:"default_ratio"`
	DefaultGap        int     `yaml:"default_gap"`
}
    SplitDefaults defines specced defaults for Split.

type Stack struct {
	Dir      StackDir
	Children []Widget
	// Measured enables constraint-based allocation for this stack. When false,
	// the historical equal-share behavior is preserved.
	Measured    bool
	Constraints []layout.Constraint
	Gap         int

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Stack arranges a fixed list of widgets vertically or horizontally.
    Each child receives an equal share of the available space; fractional pixels
    are added to the last child so dimensions always sum correctly. Focus cycles
    through children on Tab.

func NewStack(dir StackDir, children ...Widget) *Stack
    NewStack creates a Stack with the given children and direction.

func (s *Stack) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme forwards the theme to all children that implement Themeable.

func (s *Stack) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey forwards to the focused child; Tab cycles focus.

func (s *Stack) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse forwards to the child whose rect contains the event.

func (s *Stack) ConsumePaste(e PasteEvent) EventResult

func (s *Stack) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for this stack layout.

func (s *Stack) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth estimates the widest child width for horizontal composition.

func (s *Stack) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw tiles all children across r.

func (s *Stack) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget returns the last drawn active modal in the stack.

func (s *Stack) PaneRequest() (request PaneRequest)
    PaneRequest merges the terminal requirements of all children.

func (s *Stack) Tick(now time.Time)

func (s *Stack) TickInterval() (shortest time.Duration)

type StackDir int
    StackDir controls the direction a Stack or Split arranges its children.

const (
	Vertical   StackDir = iota // children stacked top-to-bottom
	Horizontal                 // children arranged left-to-right
)
type StartupConfig struct {
	Splash     *SplashController
	View       *SplashView
	Next       Widget
	Cadence    Cadence
	Transition Transition
}
    StartupConfig configures Pane.RunStartup.

    Splash is required and owns task execution and the final completed-frame
    hold. View is the widget rendered while Splash is active; when it is nil,
    a view is created from Splash's title and provider tasks. Next is the widget
    revealed after the final splash frame. Cadence controls snapshot collection
    and redraw; zero values use the splash animation interval. Transition is
    optional and defaults to an immediate handover.
