type Style struct {
	FG        Color
	BG        Color
	Bold      bool
	Underline bool
	Dim       bool
	Italic    bool
	Strike    bool
	Invert    bool
}
    Style describes the visual appearance of a Canvas cell.

func StyleForProviderState(state ProviderState) Style
    StyleForProviderState returns the visual style corresponding to a provider
    state.

func (s Style) ANSI() string
    ANSI returns the escape sequence that applies this style. Always starts with
    a full reset to avoid state bleed from previous cells.

func (s Style) ANSIFor(profile ColorProfile) string
    ANSIFor returns the style escape sequence downsampled for profile.

type StyledRows struct {
	Lines []string
}
    StyledRows renders rows of ANSI-formatted text while preserving SGR styles.
    Each input string occupies one canvas row; rows are clipped and never wrap.

func NewStyledRows(lines ...string) *StyledRows
    NewStyledRows creates a widget for the supplied ANSI-formatted rows.

func (s *StyledRows) ConsumeKey(KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey does not consume keyboard events.

func (s *StyledRows) ConsumeMouse(MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse does not consume mouse events.

func (s *StyledRows) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders styled cells into r, clipping complete display-width clusters
    at its right edge. The allocated rectangle is cleared first, so a shorter
    redraw cannot leave old text or styling behind.

type Tab struct {
	Title  string
	Widget Widget
}
    Tab pairs a title with the widget shown while that tab is active.

type Table struct {
	Columns  []Column
	Rows     []Row
	SortCol  int  // index of sorted column; -1 = none
	SortDesc bool // false = ascending ▲, true = descending ▼

	// CellCursor enables cell-by-cell selection. In this mode left/right move
	// between columns and up/down move between rows; row selection remains the
	// default when it is false.
	CellCursor bool
	// FrozenCols keeps this many leading columns visible during horizontal
	// scrolling in cell-cursor mode.
	FrozenCols int
	// OnCellSelect runs when the cell cursor moves, with filtered row and
	// column indexes.
	OnCellSelect func(row, col int)

	Prompt string
	// Placeholder is a dim hint after the prompt while the query is empty; "" disables.
	Placeholder string
	Controls    string // right-aligned hint; auto-computed from SortCol when empty
	OnSelect    func(Row)
	OnSort      func(col int, desc bool) // called when Tab or ! changes sort

	Style TableStyle

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Table is a filterable, sortable, keyboard-navigable table widget.

    Key bindings:
      - tab cycle sort column forward (or complete command in command mode)
      - ! toggle sort direction (asc ▲ / desc ▼)
      - up/down move row selection; wraps at boundaries
      - left/right move the cell cursor when CellCursor is enabled
      - pgup/pgdown (also pageup/pagedown and pgdn) move by a page of rows
      - enter confirm selection (calls OnSelect if set, otherwise quits)
      - esc/ctrl-c abort
      - : / activate command mode (see loom.Cmd, loom.Nav)
      - printable append to filter (all columns searched)
      - backspace delete last filter character

func NewTable(cols []Column, rows []Row) *Table
    NewTable creates a ready-to-use Table with default style.

func (t *Table) Aborted() bool
    Aborted reports whether the user dismissed without selecting.

func (t *Table) AddCmd(cmd Cmd)
    AddCmd registers a view-local command accessible via ':name' in this widget.

func (t *Table) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the Table style from the theme.

func (t *Table) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey drives navigation, filtering, and sort controls. ':' or '/'
    activates command mode; Tab completes commands when active.

func (t *Table) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse selects a visible data row and, in cell-cursor mode, its
    column.

func (t *Table) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height: header + rows + prompt.

func (t *Table) Draw(cv *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the table into r. Layout: r.Y = header row, r.Y+1 .. r.Y+H-2 =
    data rows, r.Y+H-1 = prompt.

func (t *Table) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether this widget is focused.

func (t *Table) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget exposes the table's command help popup, when open.

func (t *Table) Nav() Nav
    Nav returns the navigation signal set by a prompt command (:home).

func (t *Table) SearchBar() *SearchBar
    SearchBar returns the underlying SearchBar component.

func (t *Table) Selected() (Item, bool)
    Selected returns the chosen Row (wrapped in Item for paneable compatibility)
    and whether a selection was made (not aborted).

func (t *Table) SetFocus(f bool)
    SetFocus sets the focus state of this widget.

func (t *Table) SetRows(rows []Row)
    SetRows replaces the row data and re-applies the current filter. Call this
    after sorting or refreshing the underlying data.

type TableDefaults struct {
	SortAscGlyph    string `yaml:"sort_asc_glyph"`
	SortDescGlyph   string `yaml:"sort_desc_glyph"`
	ControlsHintFmt string `yaml:"controls_hint_fmt"`
}
    TableDefaults defines sort chrome for Table.

type TableStyle struct {
	Header     Style // unsorted header cells
	SortHeader Style // sorted column header (bold + underline by default)
	Normal     Style
	Selected   Style
	Prompt     Style
	// Placeholder styles the hint shown while the query is empty; it is always dim.
	Placeholder Style
	SearchBar   SearchBarStyle
}
    TableStyle controls the visual appearance of a Table.

func DefaultTableStyle() TableStyle
    DefaultTableStyle returns styles derived from the specced default theme.

type Tabs struct {
	Tabs  []Tab
	Style TabsStyle
	Keys  TabsKeys
	// Vertical places tab titles in a left column. The zero value preserves
	// the historical horizontal tab bar.
	Vertical bool
	// SwitchKey optionally cycles to the next tab in addition to left/right
	// arrow keys (e.g. "tab" or "ctrl-t"). Empty disables it.
	SwitchKey string
	// ArrowSwitch is retained for source compatibility. Arrow bindings now
	// follow the same child-first event bubbling as other tab bindings.
	ArrowSwitch bool
	OnChildQuit func(i int) (quitHost bool)

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Tabs hosts child widgets under a row of tabs, switching which child receives
    Draw/ConsumeKey/ConsumeMouse. Tabs may be added, inserted, removed,
    or replaced at runtime using its lifecycle methods.

func NewTabs(tabs ...Tab) *Tabs
    NewTabs creates a Tabs widget hosting the given tabs, analogous to NewStack.

func (t *Tabs) Add(tab Tab) int
    Add appends tab and returns its index.

func (t *Tabs) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme restyles the tab bar and forwards the theme to all children that
    implement Themeable.

func (t *Tabs) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey applies configured navigation (and SwitchKey, if set), delegating
    everything else to the active child.

func (t *Tabs) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse selects a tab on a bar click and dispatches panel events to the
    active child in child-local coordinates.

func (t *Tabs) ConsumePaste(e PasteEvent) EventResult

func (t *Tabs) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height: the tab bar plus the tallest
    child, so switching tabs does not shift the reserved layout height.

func (t *Tabs) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth estimates the widest child width, at least as wide as the
    rendered tab bar.

func (t *Tabs) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the tab bar in the top or left edge of r and the active child
    in the remaining space. The active tab is highlighted with t.Style.Active.

func (t *Tabs) Focus() int
    Focus returns the index of the currently active tab.

func (t *Tabs) HeightForWidth(width int) int
    HeightForWidth estimates preferred height at an allocated width: the tab bar
    plus the tallest child's preferred height at that width.

func (t *Tabs) Insert(index int, tab Tab) error
    Insert adds tab at index. Index may equal the current tab count to append.
    The currently selected tab remains selected.

func (t *Tabs) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget exposes only the active tab's visible modal.

func (t *Tabs) PaneRequest() (request PaneRequest)
    PaneRequest merges the terminal requirements of all tabs.

func (t *Tabs) Remove(index int) error
    Remove deletes the tab at index. Removing a tab before the selection keeps
    the same tab selected; removing the selected tab chooses its successor,
    or the preceding tab when the removed tab was last.

func (t *Tabs) Select(index int) bool
    Select activates index and reports whether it was valid.

func (t *Tabs) SetFocusIndex(i int)
    SetFocusIndex activates the tab at index i, clamping to the valid range.

func (t *Tabs) SetKeys(keys TabsKeys)
    SetKeys replaces the declarative navigation key configuration.

func (t *Tabs) SetTabs(tabs ...Tab)
    SetTabs replaces all tabs and clamps the selected index to the new bounds.

func (t *Tabs) Tick(now time.Time)
    Tick forwards the update to the active child.

func (t *Tabs) TickInterval() time.Duration
    TickInterval returns the active child's requested cadence.

type TabsKeys struct {
	Previous string
	Next     string
	Cycle    string
	Select   []string
}
    TabsKeys configures keyboard navigation for a Tabs widget. Previous, Next,
    and Cycle each name one key. Select maps keys to tab indexes by position.
    Bindings match either KeyEvent.Key or KeyEvent.Text.

func DefaultTabsKeys() TabsKeys
    DefaultTabsKeys returns the historical left/right arrow navigation.

type TabsStyle struct {
	Active   Style // active tab title (header_*)
	Inactive Style // inactive tab titles (normal_*)
	Rule     Style // bar separator rule (border_*)
}
    TabsStyle controls the visual appearance of a Tabs widget's bar.
    It reuses existing theme roles (header_* for the active tab, normal_*
    for inactive tabs, border_* for the bar rule) rather than introducing new
    spec/themes.yaml keys.

func DefaultTabsStyle() TabsStyle
    DefaultTabsStyle returns styles derived from the specced default theme.

type TextArea struct {
	Placeholder   string  // dim hint shown when the whole buffer is empty
	Keys          *KeyMap // optional action bindings; the "copy" action copies the selection or value
	StyleResolver syntax.StyleResolver
	MinHeight     int // minimum preferred content height; zero uses the content height
	MaxHeight     int // maximum preferred content height; zero is unbounded

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    TextArea is a multi-line text editor — the sibling of TextInput for bodies
    that span several lines (e.g. a git commit message body). It holds the
    text as a slice of rune lines with a (row, col) caret, scrolls vertically
    when the content exceeds the visible height, and commits nothing itself:
    the host decides when editing ends (e.g. Ctrl-D) and reads Value.

    Enter inserts a newline (splitting the current line); Backspace at column
    0 joins with the previous line; arrows/Home/End move the caret. ConsumeKey
    returns consumed=true for keys it acted on so the host keeps its own end
    key.

func NewTextArea(value string) *TextArea
    NewTextArea creates a TextArea seeded with value (split on "\n").

func (t *TextArea) Caret() (row, col int)
    Caret returns the caret position as (row, col), both rune offsets.

func (t *TextArea) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (consumed EventResult)
    ConsumeKey applies an editing key, returning consumed=true when it acted.

func (t *TextArea) ConsumePaste(event PasteEvent) EventResult
    ConsumePaste inserts a multiline paste at the caret in one buffer update.

func (t *TextArea) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight reports the content line count clamped to MinHeight and
    MaxHeight. A zero bound is ignored.

func (t *TextArea) ContentWidth() int
    ContentWidth reports the widest line in terminal cells.

func (t *TextArea) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect, focused bool)
    Draw renders the visible lines into r, scrolling so the caret stays in view,
    and — when focused — places the canvas cursor at the caret. The placeholder
    shows only when the entire buffer is empty.

func (t *TextArea) FoldedRanges() map[int]int
    FoldedRanges returns a copy of active fold ranges (startLine -> endLine).

func (t *TextArea) Highlighter() syntax.Engine
    Highlighter returns the attached syntax engine, or nil.

func (t *TextArea) IsFolded(startLine int) bool
    IsFolded reports whether a fold starting at startLine is currently
    collapsed.

func (t *TextArea) LineCount() int
    LineCount returns the number of text lines.

func (t *TextArea) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure reports the preferred content size. Width is the parent's supplied
    width when positive; height is the content line count clamped to the bounds.

func (t *TextArea) Scroll() int
    Scroll returns the vertical scroll offset in visible rows.

func (t *TextArea) SetCaret(row, col int)
    SetCaret moves the caret to (row, col), clamping to valid ranges.

func (t *TextArea) SetClipboardWriter(write func(string))
    SetClipboardWriter sets the callback used by the "copy" KeyMap action.

func (t *TextArea) SetHighlighter(h syntax.Engine)
    SetHighlighter attaches a syntax engine to the text area.

func (t *TextArea) SetSelection(start, end int)
    SetSelection selects the half-open rune range [start, end) in Value().

func (t *TextArea) SetValue(s string)
    SetValue replaces the buffer and puts the caret at the end of the last line.

func (t *TextArea) ToggleFold(startLine, endLine int)
    ToggleFold collapses or expands the fold range starting at startLine.

func (t *TextArea) Value() string
    Value returns the buffer as a single newline-joined string.

func (t *TextArea) VisibleLines() []int
    VisibleLines returns the slice of document line indices currently visible.

type TextInput struct {
	Prompt      string  // drawn before the value, e.g. "title> "
	Placeholder string  // dim hint shown when the buffer is empty
	Mask        rune    // optional display rune repeated once per value rune; zero shows the value
	Keys        *KeyMap // optional action bindings; "copy" works only when Mask is zero

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    TextInput is a single-line text editor with a movable caret. It is the
    shared editing primitive behind Settings KindString rows and wizard value
    entry: it owns a rune buffer and a caret index, and renders an optional
    prompt prefix plus a dim placeholder when empty.

    TextInput does not decide when editing starts or ends — the host widget
    calls ConsumeKey for input keys and reads Value when it wants the result.
    ConsumeKey returns consumed=true for keys it acted on (printable text,
    backspace, delete, left/right/home/end) so the host can keep navigation keys
    for itself.

func NewTextInput(value string) *TextInput
    NewTextInput creates a TextInput seeded with value.

func (t *TextInput) Caret() int
    Caret returns the current caret index (rune offset from the start).

func (t *TextInput) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (consumed EventResult)
    ConsumeKey applies an editing key. It returns consumed=true when the key
    was an editing action; copy is refused when Mask is set so masked values
    cannot be copied. The host should treat consumed=false keys (enter, esc,
    …) as its own.

func (t *TextInput) ConsumePaste(event PasteEvent) EventResult
    ConsumePaste inserts single-line paste text at the caret.

func (t *TextInput) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect, focused bool)
    Draw renders the prompt, the value (or the dim placeholder when empty) into
    r, and — when focused — sets the canvas cursor at the caret column. The host
    owns focus, so it passes focused so an unfocused field shows no cursor.

func (t *TextInput) SetClipboardWriter(write func(string))
    SetClipboardWriter sets the callback used by the "copy" KeyMap action.

func (t *TextInput) SetSelection(start, end int)
    SetSelection selects the half-open rune range [start, end).

func (t *TextInput) SetValue(s string)
    SetValue replaces the buffer and places the caret at the end.

func (t *TextInput) Value() string
    Value returns the current buffer as a string.

type ThemeColor struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    ThemeColor distinguishes the terminal default, palette indices, and RGB.
    Its zero value is the terminal default.

func DefaultThemeColor() ThemeColor
    DefaultThemeColor returns the terminal-default theme color.

func ThemeColorIndex(index uint8) ThemeColor
    ThemeColorIndex returns an indexed theme color, including palette index 0.

func ThemeColorRGB(r, g, b uint8) ThemeColor
    ThemeColorRGB returns an explicit 24-bit theme color.

func (c ThemeColor) Color() Color
    Color converts a theme color to its terminal rendering color.

func (c ThemeColor) IsDefault() bool
    IsDefault reports whether the color uses the terminal default.

func (c *ThemeColor) UnmarshalYAML(value *yaml.Node) error
    UnmarshalYAML accepts "default", #RRGGBB, or an integer palette index.

    ThemeColors is the Go representation of one theme entry in spec/themes.yaml.

func DefaultTheme() ThemeColors

    DefaultTheme. Unknown names fall back to the "plain" theme.

    from the theme.

func (t ThemeColors) ScrollbarStyle() ScrollbarStyle

func (t ThemeColors) SearchBarStyle() SearchBarStyle
    SearchBarStyle returns a SearchBarStyle derived from the theme's color
    roles.

func (t ThemeColors) TableStyle() TableStyle
    TableStyle returns a TableStyle derived from the theme's color roles.

func (t ThemeColors) TabsStyle() TabsStyle
    TabsStyle returns a TabsStyle derived from the theme's color roles.

type Themeable interface {
	Widget
	ApplyTheme(ThemeColors)
}
    Themeable is an optional interface for widgets that can restyle themselves
    from a ThemeColors set. Composite widgets forward ApplyTheme to children.

type Ticker interface {
	Widget
	TickInterval() time.Duration
	Tick(now time.Time)
}
    Ticker is an optional interface for widgets that need periodic updates.

type TickerControlAware interface {
	SetResetTick(func())
}
    TickerControlAware widgets accept a callback that resets their Pane's tick
    countdown. Call it after an action that should postpone the next tick.
    Widgets that change TickInterval should also invalidate so the Pane can
    apply the new cadence immediately.

type Timer struct {
	// Controls enables visible start/stop/reset buttons, Space to toggle, and R to reset.
	Controls  bool
	Duration  time.Duration
	Formatter DurationFormatter
	OnDone    func()
	Now       func() time.Time
	Style     Style

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Timer displays a countdown. Start, Stop and Reset control its Pane-driven
    updates; OnDone is called once when a running timer reaches zero.

func NewTimer(d time.Duration) *Timer
    NewTimer constructs a stopped countdown with duration d.

func (t *Timer) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult

func (t *Timer) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult

func (t *Timer) ContentHeight() int

func (t *Timer) ContentWidth() int

func (t *Timer) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)

func (t *Timer) Remaining() time.Duration
    Remaining reports the time remaining, clamped at zero.

func (t *Timer) Reset()
    Reset stops the timer and restores its original duration.

func (t *Timer) SetInvalidate(fn func())
    SetInvalidate implements InvalidationAware.

func (t *Timer) SetResetTick(fn func())
    SetResetTick implements TickerControlAware.

func (t *Timer) Start()
    Start starts or resumes the countdown and requests a redraw.

func (t *Timer) Stop()
    Stop pauses the countdown.

func (t *Timer) Tick(now time.Time)
    Tick updates the countdown and invokes OnDone once on completion.

func (t *Timer) TickInterval() time.Duration
    TickInterval implements Ticker. The countdown updates once per displayed
    second.

type Toggle struct {

type Transition interface {
	Enter(ctx context.Context, from, to Widget) error
}
    Transition is called once when a startup splash hands control to its
    destination widget. The callback runs on the pane event-loop goroutine,
    so implementations must return promptly.

type TransitionFunc func(context.Context, Widget, Widget) error
    TransitionFunc adapts a function to a Transition.

func (f TransitionFunc) Enter(ctx context.Context, from, to Widget) error
    Enter implements Transition.

type View struct {
	Lines      []string
	Scroll     int   // first visible line index
	OffsetX    int   // first visible display column
	OffsetY    int   // first visible line index (alias for Scroll)
	Height     int   // preferred visible height cap; 0 = len(Lines)
	Style      Style // base style for all lines
	FocusStyle Style // style for all lines when focused (falls back to Style if zero)
	Scrollbar  ScrollbarStyle
	// ScrollbarMode overrides the spec default for this widget.
	ScrollbarMode ScrollbarMode

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    View is a scrollable list of text lines rendered into a Rect. When content
    exceeds the visible area a specced scroll indicator appears on the right
    edge, proportional to the current scroll position.

func NewView(lines []string) *View
    NewView creates a View from a slice of pre-formatted lines.

func (v *View) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeKey supports line, half-page, page, and boundary navigation.

func (v *View) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) (quit EventResult)
    ConsumeMouse supports wheel navigation and clicks in the scrollbar track.

func (v *View) ContentHeight() int
    ContentHeight estimates the required height for this view.

func (v *View) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders visible lines into r. When scrollable, the rightmost column
    is reserved for the scroll indicator and content is truncated one column
    shorter.

func (v *View) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the view currently has input focus.

func (v *View) Nav() Nav
    Nav satisfies Paneable; View generates no navigation signals.

func (v *View) Offset() (x, y int)
    Offset returns the current display-column and line offsets.

func (v *View) Pan(dx, dy int)
    Pan moves the view by display columns and lines, clamping at the origin.

func (v *View) Selected() (Item, bool)
    Selected satisfies Paneable; View is read-only and yields no selection.

func (v *View) SetFocus(focused bool)
    SetFocus sets whether the view currently has input focus.

func (v *View) SetOffset(x, y int)
    SetOffset sets the view's display-column and line offsets.

type Viewport struct {
	Child         Widget
	ScrollX       int
	ScrollY       int
	ScrollbarMode ScrollbarMode
	Scrollbar     ScrollbarStyle
	Style         Style // base text and background colors

	// Has unexported fields.
}
    Viewport displays a scrollable window over a widget that can report its
    preferred content size through Measurer, ContentWidther, or ContentHeighter.

func NewViewport(child Widget) *Viewport
    NewViewport wraps child in a scrollable viewport.

func (v *Viewport) ApplyTheme(theme ThemeColors)
    ApplyTheme updates the viewport surface, scrollbar, and themeable child.

func (v *Viewport) ConsumeKey(e KeyEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeKey scrolls the viewport or forwards an unhandled key to its child.

func (v *Viewport) ConsumeMouse(e MouseEvent) EventResult
    ConsumeMouse scrolls with the wheel and translates pointer coordinates into
    the child's full content coordinate space.

func (v *Viewport) Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)
    Draw renders the measured child offscreen, then blits the visible window.

func (v *Viewport) Focused() bool
    Focused reports whether the viewport owns focus.

func (v *Viewport) Measure(width int) measure.Size
    Measure reports the viewport's natural content size.

func (v *Viewport) ModalMouseTarget() (Widget, Rect)
    ModalMouseTarget translates the child's content origin through scrolling.

func (v *Viewport) SetFocus(focused bool)
    SetFocus updates focus and forwards it to a focusable child.

type Widget interface {
	// Draw renders the widget into region r of canvas c.
	// r is guaranteed to be within c.Bounds(). Draw must not write outside r.
	Draw(c *Canvas, r Rect)

	EventConsumer
	MouseConsumer
}
    Widget is the core interface every loom UI element must satisfy.

    Pane drives a single root Widget. Composite widgets (Stack, Grid, Popup)
    implement Widget and delegate to their children.

    Lifecycle per frame:
     1. Pane clears the Canvas and calls root.Draw(canvas, canvas.Bounds()).
     2. Pane reads one event (key or mouse) from the terminal.
     3. Pane dispatches the event to the root widget.
     4. If the returned EventResult requests quit, Pane.Run returns. Done marks
        a widget interaction complete and leaves the event loop running.

func ParseASCIIGrid(gridStr string, widgets map[string]Widget) (Widget, error)
    ParseASCIIGrid parses the ASCII visual layout grid and maps widget keys to
    layout stacks.

func UnwrapWidget(widget Widget) Widget
    UnwrapWidget returns the innermost widget in a chain of wrappers.

type WidgetActivator interface {
	Activate()
}
    WidgetActivator is an optional lifecycle hook called on tab selection,
    including selection of the already active tab.

type WidgetUnwrapper interface {
	Unwrap() Widget
}
    WidgetUnwrapper exposes a wrapped widget to framework lifecycle hooks.
    Implementations should return the wrapped widget directly.

type WidthHeighter interface {
	HeightForWidth(width int) int
}
    WidthHeighter estimates preferred height at an allocated terminal-cell
    width. Resizable panes prefer this over ContentHeighter for responsive
    roots.

type WinchMeter struct {
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    WinchMeter measures SIGWINCH arrival rate over a sliding window. The window
    is also the smoothing: the rate is the event count in the window divided by
    the window length. It takes explicit timestamps so tests need no clock.

func (m *WinchMeter) Events(now time.Time) int
    Events returns the number of events inside the window ending at now.

func (m *WinchMeter) Rate(now time.Time) float64
    Rate returns events per second over the span between the first and last
    event in the window ending at now, so a fast burst is measured at once
    instead of ramping up as the window fills. Fewer than two events give 0.

func (m *WinchMeter) Record(now time.Time)
    Record notes one SIGWINCH received at now.

type YamlApp struct {
	Name   string `yaml:"name"`
	Mode   string `yaml:"mode"`
	Root   string `yaml:"root"`
	Height int    `yaml:"height"`
	MinH   int    `yaml:"min_height"`
	MaxH   int    `yaml:"max_height"`
	MaxW   int    `yaml:"max_width"`
}
    YamlApp defines global TUI properties.

type YamlConfig struct {
	App   YamlApp    `yaml:"app"`
	Pane  *YamlView  `yaml:"pane"`  // legacy fallback
	View  *YamlView  `yaml:"view"`  // single view
	Views []YamlView `yaml:"views"` // multiple views
}
    YamlConfig is the top-level container for the Loom YAML configuration.

func (c *YamlConfig) Height(contentH int) int
    Height returns the target pane height given the estimated content height.

func (c *YamlConfig) MaxWidth() int
    MaxWidth returns the target max width.

func (c *YamlConfig) RootView() (*YamlView, error)
    RootView resolves the entrypoint layout configuration.

func (c *YamlConfig) Validate() error
    Validate checks that all views, layout grids, and elements are correctly
    configured.

type YamlElement struct {
	Type        string    `yaml:"type"`
	Prompt      string    `yaml:"prompt"`
	Placeholder string    `yaml:"placeholder"`
	Cursor      string    `yaml:"cursor"`
	Unicode     string    `yaml:"unicode"`
	MaxW        int       `yaml:"max_width"`
	Controls    string    `yaml:"controls"`
	Source      string    `yaml:"source"`
	Static      yaml.Node `yaml:"static"`
	OnChange    string    `yaml:"on_change"`
	StyleName   string    `yaml:"style"`
}
    YamlElement defines a single configurable component in the YAML schema.

type YamlSetting struct {
	Name    string   `yaml:"name"`
	Kind    string   `yaml:"kind"`
	Options []string `yaml:"options"`
	Default string   `yaml:"default"`
}
    YamlSetting defines a configurable setting row inside a settings element.

type YamlView struct {
	Name     string                 `yaml:"name"`
	Title    string                 `yaml:"title"`
	Type     string                 `yaml:"type"`
	Height   int                    `yaml:"height"`
	MinH     int                    `yaml:"min_height"`
	MaxH     int                    `yaml:"max_height"`
	MaxW     int                    `yaml:"max_width"`
	Grid     string                 `yaml:"grid"`
	Elements map[string]YamlElement `yaml:"elements"`
	Order    []string               `yaml:"order"`
	Frame    *Frame                 `yaml:"frame"`
	// OnKey is retained for legacy documents; routing still uses Widget.ConsumeKey.
	OnKey map[string]string `yaml:"on_key"`
}
    YamlView defines the layout and bindings for a single TUI screen pane.
